DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.claim: Qaḍā can mean bringing death, as Pharaoh’s people ask for death and Moses’ blow kills a man.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r7.anchor: الخامس : قضى نزل الموت قوله تعالى

DAMGHANI:v1p271/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r2.claim: Shīʿa can mean an army: one of the two men was from Moses’ army.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r2.anchor: الثاني الشيعة الجيش قوله تعالى في سورة القصص فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r10.claim: In the story of Moses, المدينة means Egypt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p560/r10.anchor: الثاني : مصر . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص : ﴿ ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها ﴾

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r4.claim: Al-madīnah here is the actual city and elite capital, distinct from the Israelites’ separate settlement as slaves and servants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r4.anchor: the actual city which was the centre and capital

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r5.claim: Moses’ honor and courage, traits of piety and knowledge, led him to visit secretly to see his oppressed people; the Copts feared him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r5.anchor: reflection of piety and knowledge appeared in him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p530/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p530/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p530/r1.claim: Moses intervened when an Israelite asked for help against a Copt; while trying to separate them, he struck the Copt unintentionally and the man died.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p530/r1.anchor: punched him and such was the strength of the punch that the Copt died on the spot

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the city Moses entered as Memphis; reports place Pharaoh's visit there at noon or between evening prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the city was Egypt itself; Moses had openly opposed Pharaoh and entered in disguise, wary and unseen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r2.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: المدينة مصر بنفسها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had expelled Moses, who returned after years away when people had forgotten him; other reports suggest a festival, a palace exit, Heliopolis, Habin, or Alexandria.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: كان فرعون قد أخرجه من المدينة، فغاب عنها سنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r4.claim: Abu Talib reads حين with an accusative n and explains the unusual construction as treating the noun like a verb because it is followed by a past-tense clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو طالب القارئ: على حين، بنصب نون حين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r5.claim: Naim ibn Maysara reads يقتلان by assimilating the ta letters; the men may fight over religion or over a Copt forcing an Israelite to carry Pharaoh's firewood. The verb may describe the men or be circumstantial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r5.anchor: وقرأ نعيم بن ميسرة: يقتلان. بإدغام التاء في التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r6.claim: The Israelite is Moses' religious adherent, possibly the Samaritan; the Copt is his enemy, reportedly named Fatun. Demonstratives can stage absent past figures as present, as al-Mubarrad notes with a poetic example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r6.anchor: هذا من شيعته: أي ممن شايعه على دينه، وهو الإسرائيلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r7.claim: The majority read استغاثه as asking Moses for rescue; Sibawayh, Ibn Miqsam, and al-Zafarani read استعنانه as asking for aid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فاستغاثه، أي طلب غوثه ونصره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم يوسف بن علي بن جبارة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jabbarah chooses Ibn Miqsam's aid-reading; Ibn Atiyya calls it a scribal error, but the author rejects that charge because Ibn Khalawayh and others transmit it from named readers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.anchor: والاختيار قراءة ابن مقسم، لأن الإعانة أولى في هذا الباب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.claim: A report says the Copt threatened to burden Moses with carrying wood; enraged and physically strong, Moses struck him and he died. Other readings use لكزه or نكزه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.anchor: فاشتد غضب موسى، وكان قد أوتي قوة، فوكزه، فمات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r3.claim: Qatada says Moses struck the Copt with his staff; other authorities say he used his fist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: وكزه بعصاه وغيره قال: بجمع كفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r4.claim: The subject of فقضى may be Moses, God, or the blow understood from وكزه; Moses did not intend to kill, but the blow coincided with the man's appointed death, and he regretted it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r4.anchor: وكان موسى لم يتعمد قتله، ولكن وافقت وكزته الأجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a prophet may not kill unless commanded; Ka'b says Moses was twelve and killed accidentally because a blow ordinarily does not kill; al-Naqqash says this preceded prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن جريج: ليس لنبي أن يقتل ما لم يؤمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r6.claim: Moses calls the killing Satan's work because anger led to the fatal blow, names it a wrong against himself, and seeks forgiveness; he had no authorization to kill the man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r6.anchor: وجعله من عمل الشيطان وسماه ظلما لنفسه واستغفر منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r7.claim: Moses follows Adam's language of self-wronging; the ba in بما أنعمت may be an oath with an omitted answer or depend on an omitted plea for protection through God's favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p292#2/r7.anchor: وقد انتهج موسى عليه السلام نهج آدم عليه السلام إذ قال: ظلمنا أنفسنا

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n13/r1.claim: The phrase means that the city's people were unaware at that time.
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n13/r1.anchor: Lit., "at a time of its people's unawareness"

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n14/r1.claim: Moses' phrase ‘his own people’ refers to the Hebrews.

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r1.claim: Asad links ‘Satan's doing’ to his note on 15:17; verses 16–17 show that the Israelite, rather than the Egyptian, was in the wrong.
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r1.anchor: Regarding the reference to "Satan's doing", see first half of note 16 on 15:17

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r2.claim: Moses instinctively helped his fellow Israelite from racial kinship without judging the case, then recognized he had killed an innocent person and acted from tribal prejudice.
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r2.anchor: Moses had come to the assistance of the Israelite out of an instinctive sense of racial kinship

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r3.speaker: the Prophet
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r3.claim: The Prophet condemned proclaiming, fighting, or dying for tribal partisanship; Abu Da'ud reports this on Jubayr ibn Mut'im's authority.
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r3.anchor: the Prophet on many occasions: cf. his famous saying, "He is not of us who proclaims the cause

ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r4.speaker: the Prophet
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r4.claim: The Prophet defined tribal partisanship as helping one's own people in an unjust cause; Abu Da'ud reports this on Wathilah ibn al-Asqa's authority.
ASAD-NOTES:28:15#n15/r4.anchor: the Prophet answered, "It means helping thine own people in an unjust cause"

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r8.claim: A report says Moses entered at midday during the townspeople’s rest, saw an Israelite and a Copt fighting, and struck the Copt after the Israelite sought help, causing his death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r8.anchor: İsrâilli’nin kendisinden yardım istemesi üzerine Kıptî’ye bir yumruk vurarak ölümüne sebep olmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r9.claim: Exegetes interpreted the verse in various ways to establish that Moses was sinless.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r9.anchor: Tefsirlerde Hz. Mûsâ’nın günahsız olduğunu göstermek için 15. âyeti çeşitli şekillerde yorumlayanlar olmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r10.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r10.claim: Shawkani says prophets are protected from major sins, not minor ones, and Moses’s unintentional killing was therefore not a major sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r10.anchor: Şevkânî bu yorumların, “Peygamberler günah işlemekten mâsumdur” prensibine dayandığını, ancak peygamberlerin (küçük günah değil) büyük günah işlemekten mâsum bulunduklarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r11.claim: Moses intervened because an oppressed person sought help, so the intervention itself was blameless.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r11.anchor: Bize göre Hz. Mûsâ’nın kavgaya müdahalesi hor görülen ve ezilen topluluktan birinin imdat istemesi üzerine olmuştur ve bunda kusur yoktur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r12.claim: Moses intended only a careless slap or punch, and such a blow rarely causes death; his act can be understood as unintended manslaughter and even a virtue of siding with the weak.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r12.anchor: Yaptığı şey, sadece tedbirsizlikle bir tokat veya yumruk vurmaktı. Böyle bir darbenin ölüm sonucunu doğurması nâdirdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r13.claim: Moses felt guilty because his act caused a death, while his reference to Satan shows he had no evil intent; judging right and wrong during a fight is difficult.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r13.anchor: Mûsa’nın kendisini günahkâr görmesi, fiilinin ölüme sebep olmasındandır. 15. âyete göre Mûsâ’nın şeytana gönderme yapması da kötü kastının olmadığını gösterir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r14.claim: Moses had not yet become a prophet, and the Torah was revealed much later, after the Israelites left Egypt for Sinai.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r14.anchor: Özellikle Tevrat’ın çok daha sonra, İsrâiloğulları’nı Mısır’dan Sînâ çölüne geçirmesinin ardından inzâl edildiği bilinmektedir.

BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r1.claim: Moses entered Misr after coming from Pharaoh's palace, which stood at the city's edge.
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r1.anchor: ودخل موسى مصرا آتيا من قصر فرعون

BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r2.claim: The author links the palace's location to the later reference to a man arriving from the far side of the city.
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r2.anchor: كما سيأتي عند قوله تعالى : {وجآء رجل من أقصا المدينة} (القصص : 20)

BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r3.claim: Some identify the city as Memphis, Pharaoh's residence: it lay west of the Nile, twelve miles from old Cairo, and was Egypt's royal seat and earliest post-Flood city.
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r3.anchor: قيل المراد مدينة منف من أرض مصر وهي مدينة فرعون موسى

BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r4.claim: The time was one when people did not normally enter the city.
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r4.anchor: أي حال كونه في وقت لا يعتاد دخولها

BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses entered at midday during the customary rest, when the roads were empty.
BURSEVI:v6p283#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : دخلها في الظهيرة عند المقيل وقد خلت الطرق

BURSEVI:v6p284/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r1.claim: The clause about the two men fighting describes رجلين as an adjective clause.

BURSEVI:v6p284/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r2.claim: The verb form اقتتال means that the men fought one another.

BURSEVI:v6p284/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r3.claim: The man from Moses's faction was one who followed him in religion, namely an Israelite.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r3.anchor: أي ممن شايعه وتابعه على دينه وهم بنو إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v6p284/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r4.claim: Fath al-Rahman reports that the Israelite was the Samaritan.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r4.anchor: روي أنه السامري كما في "فتح الرحمن"

BURSEVI:v6p284/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r5.claim: The demonstrative wording retells the scene: the men were not present when the Prophet heard the account, but were present when Moses encountered them.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r5.anchor: والإشارة على الحكاية وإلا فهو والذي من عدوه ما كانا حاضرين حال الحكاية لرسول الله

BURSEVI:v6p284/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r6.claim: Moses's religious opponents were Copts; Kashf al-Asrar names this man Fatun and says he was Pharaoh's baker trying to force an Israelite to carry wood to the royal kitchen.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r6.anchor: وهم القبط واسمه فاتون كما في "كشف الأسرار" وكان خباز فرعون

BURSEVI:v6p284/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r7.claim: The Israelite asked Moses for help against the Copt; على governs the request because استغاث means seeking aid or support.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r7.anchor: أي سأله أن يغيثه بالإعانة عليه ولذلك عدي بعلي يقال : استغثت طلبت الغوث

BURSEVI:v6p284/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r8.claim: Moses had been given strength and power.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r8.anchor: وكان موسى قد أعطي شدة وقوة

BURSEVI:v6p284/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284/r9.claim: The Persian gloss says Moses told the Copt to release the man, but the Copt rejected Moses's words.
BURSEVI:v6p284/r9.anchor: قبطي راكفت دست ازو بدار قبطي سخن موسى ردكرد

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r1.claim: Wakz can mean pushing, thrusting, or striking with the closed fist; Moses struck the Copt with his fist.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r1.anchor: الوكز كالوعد الدفع والطعن والضرب بجمع الكف

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r2.claim: Moses killed the Copt, regretted it, and buried him in sand; قضيت عليه can also mean finishing or completing something.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r2.anchor: أي : فقتله فندم فدفنه في الرمل وكل شيء فرغت وأتممته فقد قضيت عليه

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r3.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that death is expressed with القضاء, as in completing one's allotted term, since it ends one's distinct worldly affair.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r3.anchor: في "المفردات" : يعبر عن الموت بالقضاء فيقضى نحبه لأنه فصل أمره بالمختص به

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r4.claim: Moses attributes the killing to Satan because it arose through Satan's misleading and whispering.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r4.anchor: فأضيف العمل إلى الشيطان لأنه كان بإغوائه ووسوسته

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r5.claim: It was Satan's work because Moses had not been ordered to kill unbelievers, or because he was safe among them and should not have assassinated one.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r5.anchor: وإنما كان من عمله لأنه لم يؤمر بقتل الكفار أو لأنه كان مأمونا فيهم

BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r6.claim: Calling the act injustice and asking forgiveness does not compromise infallibility: it was an error before prophethood, and the elect magnify even minor lapses.
BURSEVI:v6p284#2/r6.anchor: ولا يقدح ذلك في عصمته لكونه خطأ وإنما عده من عمل الشيطان وسماه ظلما واستغفر منه

BURSEVI:v6p284#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p284#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p284#3/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to Satan, Adam's enemy and an evident adversary who leads people astray.
BURSEVI:v6p284#3/r1.anchor: لابن آدم {مضل مبين} ظاهر العداوة والإضلال.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r1.claim: Qatadah places Moses’ arrival during the city’s period of neglect at midday, while people were sleeping.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ على حين غفلة من أهلها ﴾ قال عند القائلة بالظهيرة وهم نائمون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r2.claim: Qatadah says the man seeking help was an Israelite who enlisted Moses against an enemy; Moses struck the enemy with his staff and killed him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه ﴾ قال كان الذي استغاثه رجلا من بني إسرائيل

QASHANI:28:15-16/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r1.claim: The city is the body, entered when its psychic powers are quiet, lest they dominate the heart.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r1.anchor: أي: في حال هدو القوى النفسانية وسكونها حذرا من استيلائها عليه وعلوها

QASHANI:28:15-16/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r2.claim: The two combatants are intellect and passion; intellect belongs to Moses' party, while passion follows satanic fancy and the commanding lower self.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r2.anchor: أي: العقل والهوى { هذا } أي: العقل

QASHANI:28:15-16/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r3.claim: Intellect seeks the heart's aid against passion, and the heart strikes passion through practical wisdom and angelic support, using its practical rational faculty.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r3.anchor: العقل واستنصره على الهوى { فوكزه } ضربه بهيئة من هيئات الحكمة العملية

QASHANI:28:15-16/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r4.claim: Calling the conflict satanic means Satan prompted passion to transgress and aggress.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r4.anchor: الاستيلاء والاقتتال { من عمل الشيطان } الباعث للهوى على التعدي والعدوان

QASHANI:28:15-16/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r5.claim: Alternatively, the killing itself is satanic because excess is treated through the opposite vice of deficiency rather than merciful justice; both extremes are vices.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r5.anchor: لأن علاج الاستيلاء بالإفراط لا يكون بالفضيلة التي هي العدالة الفائضة من الرحمن

QASHANI:28:15-16/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:15-16/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:15-16/r6.claim: Examples of satanic treatment by opposite extremes are checking greed with lethargy, miserliness with extravagance, and wastefulness with stinginess.
QASHANI:28:15-16/r6.anchor: كعلاج الشره بالخمود وعلاج البخل بالتبذير والإسراف بالتقتير كلاهما من الشيطان

QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r4.claim: Moses entered at midday while people were dispersed; he found an Israelite follower fighting an Egyptian opponent, and the Israelite asked him for help.
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r4.anchor: دخل المدينة في وقت الهاجرة ، وتفرق الناس ، فوجد فيها رجلين يتخاصمان

QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r5.claim: Moses struck the Egyptian to push him away from the Israelite, without intending to kill him, but the man died from the blow.
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r5.anchor: فوكزه موسى ليدفعه عن الإسرائيلي ، فمات الرجل بذلك الوكز ، ولم يكن موسى يقصد قتله

QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r6.claim: Moses called the harsh blow Satan’s work; he did not attribute the killing itself to Satan, but wished he had pushed the man more gently because Satan prompted his severity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r6.anchor: ولم ينسب القتل إلى الشيطان ، ولكن دفعه عنه بالغلظة نسبه إلى الشيطان بأن حمله على تلك الحدة

QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r7.claim: When God wills an outcome, He creates its causes; the Egyptian’s death from one blow fulfilled the decree, since many blows and lashes may leave someone alive.
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r7.anchor: إذا أراده الله أمرا أجرى أسبابا ليحصل بها مراده

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the city as Memphis.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس على ما في البحر : هي منف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r2.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās places the entrance at midday, while another places it between evening and nightfall, when Pharaoh’s journey to that city gave Moses an opportunity to enter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r2.anchor: وكان على ما روي عن الحبر وقت القائلة وفي رواية أخرى عنه بين العشاء والعتمة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies the city as Egypt and says Moses entered disguised after openly opposing Pharaoh and his people, then hiding away.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق : هي مصر كان موسى عليه السلام قد بدت منه مجاهرة لفرعون وقومه بما يكرهون فاختفى وغاب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had expelled Moses; after years away, Moses returned when the people had forgotten him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : كان فرعون قد أخرجه منها فغاب سنين فنسي فجاء ودخلها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r5.claim: Other reported possibilities are that Moses entered during a festival, left Pharaoh’s palace for Egypt at midday or between the two evening prayers, or entered the city of ʿAyn Shams.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : دخل في يوم عيد وهم مشغولون بلهوهم وقيل : خرج من قصر فرعون ودخل مصر وقت القيلولة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r6.claim: Further opinions identify the city as Ḥābīn, a village two leagues from Egypt, or Alexandria.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : قرية على فرسخين من مصر يقال لها : حابين وقيل : هي الاسكندرية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r7.claim: Egypt is the best-known identification and probably the most apparent one.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r7.anchor: والأشهر أنها مصر ولعله هو الأظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r8.claim: The most immediate syntax links على حين to دخل, with على meaning “in,” as in the cited usage about Solomon’s reign.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r8.anchor: والمتبادر أن على حين متعلق بدخل وعليه فالظاهر أن على بمعنى في مثلها في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r9.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ instead treats the phrase as a circumstantial qualifier of either the city or the entering subject, the latter meaning that Moses entered furtively.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : هو في موضع الحال من المدينة ويجوز أن يكون في موضع الحال من الفاعل أي مختلسا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the circumstantial analyses depart from the obvious construction to avoid reading على as “in” or explaining why the preposition was used instead of a bare adverb.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r10.anchor: ولعل الذي دعاه إلى العدول عن المتبادر احتياجه إلى جعل على بمعنى في وخفاء نكتة التعبير بها دونها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r11.claim: A further objection to the obvious reading is that entering at a time of people’s inattention does not necessarily mean that Moses entered while they were themselves inattentive.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : إن الداعي إلى ذلك أن دخول المدينة في حين غفلة من أهلها ليس نصا في دخولها غافلا أهلها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the objection is debatable because midday or the time between evening prayers may not actually be inattentive periods.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52#2/r12.anchor: كما في وجه الحالية من الضمير فان وقت الغفلة كوقت القائلة وما بين العشائين قد لايغفل فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r1.claim: من أهلها is an adjective qualifying غفلة; the indefinite form is more eloquent than an annexed phrase because its nunation conveys magnification.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r1.anchor: و ( من أهلها ) في موضع الصفة لغفلة وما في النظم الكريم أبلغ من غفلة أهلها بالاضافة لما في التنوين من إفادة التفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r2.speaker: أبو طالب القارئ
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r2.claim: Abū Ṭālib al-Qāriʾ read حين with fatḥa, explained either by neighboring غفلة or by treating the verbal noun as a verb and building حين as with a past-tense clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو طالب القاريء على حين بفتح النون ووجه بأنه فتح لمجاورة الغين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī regards the proposed grammatical explanation of the unusual حين reading as unconvincing.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r4.claim: The two men were fighting; the sentence qualifies رجلين, though Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats it as a circumstantial clause on the basis of Sībawayh’s allowance for a circumstantial clause from an indefinite noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r4.anchor: أي يتحاربان والجملة صفة للرجلين وقال ابن عطية : في موضع الحال وهو مبني على مذهب سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r5.speaker: نعيم بن ميسرة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r5.claim: Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read يقتلان with assimilation of the two tāʾs and transfer of the first vowel to qāf.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r5.anchor: وقرأ نعيم بن ميسرة يقتلان بادغام التاء في التاء ونقل فتحتها إلى القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r6.claim: The Israelite was one of Moses’s adherents, either a follower in his cause and commands or, as a group of commentators say, a fellow Israelite in religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r6.anchor: أي ممن شايعه وتابعه في أمره ونهيه أو في الدين على ما قاله جماعة وهم بنو إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r7.speaker: الاتقان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r7.claim: Al-Itqān identifies the Israelite as the Samaritan.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r8.claim: The Egyptian was Moses’s enemy, either an opponent of his aims or, according to the commentators, an unbeliever from the Copts.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r8.anchor: وهذا من عدوه من مخالفيه فيما يريد أو في الدين على ما قاله الجماعة وهم القبط

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r9.speaker: الاتقان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r9.claim: Al-Itqān gives the Egyptian’s name as Qānūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r9.anchor: واسمه كما في الاتقان أيضا قانون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r10.claim: The demonstrative is a descriptive clause qualifying each man, and it narrates what Moses saw at the time rather than addressing the Prophet in the narrative frame.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r10.anchor: صفة بعد صفة لرجلين والاشارة بهذا واقعة على طريق الحكاية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r11.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r11.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Arabic speakers can use هذا to point to someone absent; Jarīr’s verse about his cousin in Damascus illustrates the usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r11.anchor: وقال المبرد : العرب تشير بهذا إلى الغائب قال جرير : هذا ابن عمي في دمشق خليفة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r12.claim: The demonstrative itself links the description back to the men, and coordination precedes the adjectival qualification.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r12.anchor: وهذ الاشارة قائمة مقام الضمير في الربط والعطف سابق على الوصفية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r13.claim: The two men’s fight may have concerned religion or a worldly matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r13.anchor: واختلف في سبب تقاتل هذين الرجلين فقيل : كان أمرا دينيا وقيل : كان أمرا دنيويا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r14.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that the Copt, Pharaoh’s baker, demanded that an Israelite carry firewood to Pharaoh’s kitchen; the Israelite refused and they fought.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53/r14.anchor: روي أن القبطي كلف الاسرائيلي حمل الحطب إلى مطبخ فرعون فأبى فاقتتلا لذلك وكان القبطي على ما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير خبازا لفرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r1.claim: استغاثه means seeking his rescue and support against the enemy; the preposition على reflects the verb’s sense of victory or support, as confirmed by “he sought his aid yesterday.”
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r1.anchor: ولتضمين الفعل معنى النصر عدي بعلى ويؤيده قوله تعالى بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, على reflects the sense of giving assistance, supported by the variant استعانه.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تعديته بعلى لتضمينه معنى الاعانة ويؤيده أنه قريء فاستعانه بالعين المهملة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r3.claim: Ibn Khālawayh transmits the استعانه reading from Sībawayh, as do Abū al-Qāsim Yūsuf ibn ʿAlī ibn Jabbāra from Ibn Muqsam and al-Zaʿfarānī.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r3.anchor: وقد نقل هذه القراءة ابن خالويه عن سيبويه وابو القاسم يوسف بن علي بن جبارة عن ابن مقسم والزعفراني

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says al-Akhfash mentioned the reading, but al-Ālūsī says Ibn ʿAṭiyya has no basis for that attribution and it is not a valid reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r4.anchor: وقول ابن عطية أنه ذ : رها الأخفش وهو تصحيف لا قراءة مما لا ثبت له فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r5.claim: The relative clauses omit their subjects: “the one who is from his party” and “the one who is from his enemy.”
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r5.anchor: وقد حذف من جملة الصلة صدرها أي الذي هو من شيعته والذي هو من عدوه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid explains Moses’s وَكَز as striking the Copt with the closed fist, fingers together in the palm.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r6.anchor: أي ضرب القبطي بجمع كفه أي بكفه المضمومة أصابعها على ما أخرجه غير واحد عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān defines وَكَز as striking with the hand while its fingers are gathered, like a three-and-seventy knot.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الوكز الضرب باليد مجموعة أصابعها كعقد ثلاثة وسبعين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r8.claim: Qatāda says Moses struck the man with a staff; al-Ālūsī suggests he means another staff, since Moses’s famous staff came from Shuʿayb after this incident.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وجماعة عن قتادة أنه عليه السلام ضربه بعصاه فكأنه يفسر الوكز بالدفع أو الطعن

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r9.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh read فلكزه, while another reading from him is فنكزه.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله فلكزه باللام وعنه فنكزه بالنون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r10.claim: Lexicographers variously define لكز as وَكَز or a blow to the chest or palate, نكز as striking or pushing, and all three terms as pushing with the fingertips; another distinction assigns وَكَز to the heart and لكز to the jaw.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r10.anchor: واللكز على ما في القاموس الوكز والوجء في الصدر والحنك والنكز على ما فيه أيضا الضرب والدفع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r11.claim: A narrative says the Egyptian threatened to make Moses carry the firewood, enraging Moses, who had been given great strength, and he struck him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r11.anchor: روي أنه لما اشتد التناكر قال القبطي لموسى عليه السلام : لقد هممت أن أحمله يعني الحطب عليك فاشتد غضب موسى عليه السلام وكان قد أوتي قوة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r12.claim: قضى عليه means that Moses killed him: literally, he brought the man’s life to its end; the verb needs no interpretive paraphrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r12.anchor: أي فقتله موسى وأصله أنهى حياته أي جعلها منتهية متقضية وهو بهذا المعنى يتعدى بعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r13.claim: The apparent subject of قضى is Moses; the alternatives make God the subject, meaning He decreed death, or make the implied blow the subject, meaning it ended the man’s life.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r13.anchor: وعود ضمير الفاعل في قضى على موسى هو الظاهر وقيل : هو عائد على الله تعالى أي فقضى الله سبحانه عليه بالموت

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r14.claim: The verb can also take إلى through the sense of conveying or revealing, as in the cited verse about God conveying the matter to Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r14.anchor: وقد يتعدى الفعل بالى لتضمينه معنى الايحاء كما في قوله تعالى : ( وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r15.claim: “This is from Satan’s work” means Satan’s prompting or embellishment; the alternative says it is of the same kind as Satan’s work, and the first better fits the following description of Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p53#2/r15.anchor: وقيل : من جنس عمله والأول أوفق بقوله تعالى : إنه عدو مضل مبين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r1.claim: مبين is a second adjective of عدو and means that Satan’s enmity is manifest.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r1.anchor: أي ظاهر العداوة على أن مبين صفة ثانية لعدو

ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r2.claim: Another analysis takes مبين to describe both the manifest enmity and the misguidance, either by implicit wording with عدو or by one adjective shared by عدو and مضل.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r2.anchor: وقيل ظاهر العداوة والاضلال ووجه بأنه صفة لعدو الملاحظ معه وصف الاضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r3.claim: On either syntactic analysis, مبين derives from the intransitive form أبان.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p54/r3.anchor: وإيا ما كان فمبين من أبان اللازم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r1.claim: Moses entered the city; al-Suddi identifies it as Memphis in Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r1.anchor: قال السدي: هي مدينة "منف" من أرض مصر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r2.claim: Muqatil identifies the city as the village of Habin, two farsakhs from Egypt; another view identifies it as Ayn al-Shams.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كانت قرية "حابين" على رأس فرسخين من مصر. وقيل: مدينة "عين الشمس"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r3.claim: One explanation of the inattentive time is midday, when people were occupied with their nap.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r4.claim: He says Moses entered between sunset and nightfall.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r4.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: دخلها فيما بين المغرب والعشاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r5.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses, known as Pharaoh’s son, wore his clothes and rode his mounts; after Pharaoh rode without him, Moses followed and entered Memphis at midday when its outskirts were empty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r5.anchor: كان يسمى ابن فرعون، فكان يركب مراكب فرعون ويلبس مثل ملابسه، فركب فرعون يوما وليس عنده موسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses had Israelite followers and, after recognizing the truth, broke with Pharaoh’s people; their estrangement and mutual fear made him enter towns secretly and fearfully.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r6.anchor: كان لموسى شيعة من بني إسرائيل يستمعون منه ويقتدون به، فلما عرف ما هو عليه من الحق رأى فراق فرعون وقومه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had nearly killed Moses as a child after a staff incident, but his wife intervened and Pharaoh expelled him; after Moses grew up and they had forgotten him, he entered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p196/r7.anchor: لما علا موسى فرعون بالعصا في صغره، فأراد فرعون قتله، قالت امرأته: هو صغير، فترك قتله وأمر بإخراجه من مدينته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r1.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r1.claim: Ali says the time of inattention was the people’s festival, when they were occupied with amusement and play.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r1.anchor: وروي عن علي في قوله: "حين غفلة" كان يوم عيد لهم قد اشتغلوا بلهوهم ولعبهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r2.claim: The two men were arguing and quarrelling; one belonged to Moses’s Israelites and the other to his enemy, the Copts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r2.anchor: {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان} يختصمان ويتنازعان، {هذا من شيعته} بني إسرائيل، {وهذا من عدوه} من القبط،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r3.claim: One report identifies the Israelite as the Samiri and the Copt as Pharaoh’s cook, named Falyathun.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r3.anchor: قيل: الذي كان من شيعته السامري، والذي من عدوه من القبط، قيل: طباخ فرعون اسمه فليثون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r4.claim: Another explanation takes “his faction” and “his enemy” to mean a believer and a disbeliever; the Copt was forcing the Israelite to carry wood to the kitchen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r4.anchor: قيل: "هذا من شيعته. وهذا من عدوه" أي: هذا مؤمن وهذا كافر، وكان القبطي يسخر الإسرائيلي ليحمل الحطب إلى المطبخ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn Abbas that, when Moses came of age, Pharaoh’s household stopped oppressing Israelites because they knew Moses was one of them, though the public thought he was only connected through nursing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: لما بلغ موسى أشده لم يكن أحد من آل فرعون يخلص إلى أحد من بني إسرائيل بظلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r6.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s account, an Israelite appealed to Moses against a Pharaoh’s man who had seized him to carry firewood; Moses became angry, demanded his release, and the Egyptian threatened to make Moses carry it instead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r6.anchor: فاستغاثه الإسرائيلي على الفرعوني، والاستغاثة: طلب الغوث، فغضب موسى واشتد غضبه؛ لأنه تناوله وهو يعلم منزلة موسى من بني إسرائيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r7.claim: Moses had great physical size, strength, and force.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r7.anchor: وكان موسى قد أوتي بسطة في الخلق وشدة في القوة والبطش،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “fawakahahu” as “falakazahu”; the two readings have the same meaning, striking with the closed hand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: "فلكزه موسى"، ومعناهما واحد، وهو الضرب بجمع الكف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r9.claim: Another view distinguishes the verbs: “wakz” is a blow to the chest, while “lakz” is a blow to the back.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r9.anchor: وقيل: "الوكز" الضرب في الصدر و"اللكز" في الظهر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r10.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r10.claim: Al-Farra says the two verbs have the same meaning, namely pushing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: معناهما واحد، وهو الدفع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r11.claim: Abu ʿUbayda defines “wakz” as pushing with the fingertips.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الوكز الدفع بأطراف الأصابع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r12.claim: One tafsir says Moses made a fist of eighty-three and struck the man’s chest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r12.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير: عقد موسى ثلاثا وثمانين وضربه في صدره،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r13.claim: “He finished him” means Moses killed him; the verb can mean completing or finishing something.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r13.anchor: {فقضى عليه} أي: فقتله وفرغ من أمره، وكل شيء فرغت منه فقد قضيته وقضيت عليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r14.claim: Moses regretted the killing, which he had not intended, buried the man in sand, and called it Satan’s work and manifest misguidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p197/r14.anchor: فندم موسى عليه السلام، ولم يكن قصده القتل، فدفنه في الرمل، {قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين} أي: بين الضلالة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r1.claim: The city is Egypt, reached from Pharaoh's palace; other identifications given are Manf, Hāʾīn, or Ain Shams in its vicinity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r1.anchor: ودخل مصر آتيا من قصر فرعون وقيل منف أو حائين

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r2.claim: The time was one when entering was unusual and unexpected; views identify it as the midday nap or between the evening prayers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r2.anchor: في وقت لا يعتاد دخولها ولا يتوقعونه فيه، قيل كان وقت القيلولة وقيل بين العشاءين

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r3.claim: The Israelite belonged to Moses' religious community, while the Copt opposed it; the labels are from the narrative's perspective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r3.anchor: أحدهما ممن شايعه على دينه وهم بنو إسرائيل والآخر من مخالفيه وهم القبط

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r4.claim: The Israelite asked Moses to help against the Copt, which explains using على with the verb; another reading is استعانه.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r4.anchor: فسأله أن يغيثه بالإعانة ولذلك عدى ب { على } وقرىء «استعانه»

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r5.claim: Moses struck the Copt with the fist of his hand; another reading means he struck his chest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r5.anchor: فضرب القبطي بجمع كفه، وقرىء فلكزه أي فضرب به صدره

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r6.claim: To finish him means to end his life, as in the verse about completing a matter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r6.anchor: فقتله وأصله فأنهى حياته من قوله وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r7.claim: Calling the killing Satan's work may mean Moses had no command to kill unbelievers or that he had been safe among them and should not have assassinated them; it does not undermine his protection from sin because it was an error, and prophets magnify small lapses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r7.anchor: لأنه لم يؤمر بقتل الكفار أو لأنه كان مأمونا فيهم فلم يكن له اغتيالهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r8.claim: Satan is plainly hostile and misleading.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:15/r8.anchor: { إنه عدو مضل مبين } ظاهر العداوة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r1.claim: The account turns from Moses' preparation for prophethood to the event that would cause his migration, a pattern said to have begun after Abraham.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r1.anchor: وكأنها سنت بعد إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام فقال : { و خل المدينة }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r2.claim: Moses entered Pharaoh's city from the palace, where Pharaoh treated him like a son.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r2.anchor: أي مدينة فرعون آتيا من قصره , لأنه كان عنده بمنزلة الولد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir identifies the city as Memphis in Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r3.anchor: قال ابن جرير : وهي مدينة منف من مصر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r4.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r4.claim: Al-Baghawi gives Ain al-Shams as an alternative identification of the city, while noting other views.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r4.anchor: وقال البغوي : وقيل : عين الشمس . وقيل غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r5.claim: The moment of heedlessness served as a means of removing Moses from the company of the oppressive people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r5.anchor: أي إحكاما لما جعلناه سببا لنقلته منها طهارة من عشرة القوم الظالمين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r6.claim: The two men were an Israelite and an Egyptian Copt, already grappling, strangling, and striking in acts leading toward murder.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r6.anchor: أي يفعلان مقدمات القتل من الملازمة مع الخنق والضرب , وهما إسرائيلي وقبطي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r7.claim: Moses' Israelite community had gained honor because he was the king's foster child and his wet nurse was one of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r7.anchor: وكان قد حصل لبني غسرائيل به عز لكونه ربيب الملك , مع أن مرضعته منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r8.claim: The Israelite appealed to Moses to rescue him from his Coptic enemy.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r8.anchor: أي طلب منه { الذي من شيعته } أن يغيثه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r9.claim: The verb for Moses' blow can mean thrusting or pushing with his hand, striking with his whole palm like a punch, or pushing with his fingertips.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r9.anchor: فركز أي فطعن ودفع بيده العدو أو ضربه بجميع كفه , وكأنه كالكم , أو دفعه بأطراف أصابعه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r10.claim: Moses was exceptionally strong in both innate and spiritual power.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r10.anchor: وهو رجل ايد لم يعط أحد من أهل ذلك الزمان مثل ما أعطي من القوى الذاتية والمعنوية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r11.claim: To settle the man meant to impose the true judgment of death, from which no human can escape; Moses killed him and was finished with him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r11.anchor: أي فأوقع القضاء الذي هو القضاء على الحقيقة , وهو الموت الذي لا ينجو منه بشر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r12.claim: No one noticed the killing because the people were heedless.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r12.anchor: وخفي هذا على الناس لما هم فيه من الغفلة , فلم يشعر به أحد منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r13.claim: Moses called the act Satan's work because he had received no specific command to do it and had not intended it, even though the slain man was an unbeliever.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p471/r13.anchor: أي لأني لم أومر به على الخصوص , ولم يكن نقصدي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r1.claim: Satan is an enemy who misleads and whose hostility and misguidance are unmistakable.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r1.anchor: ومع كونه عدوا ينبغي الحذر منه فهو { مضل } لا يقود إلى خير أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r2.claim: Moses regretted killing the man because he lacked a specific authorization, not because the killing was impermissible; perceptive people expect prophets to magnify even lapses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p472/r2.anchor: لم يأته في قتله إذن خاص , وكان قد أخبر عنه بالندم

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r1.claim: The narrative places the city at Manf (Memphis): Moses arrived around midday, when its markets had closed and its streets were empty.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r1.anchor: فأدركه المقيل بأرض يقال لها منف فدخلها نصف النهار وقد تغلقت أسواقها وليس في طرقها أحد

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the time when Moses entered as midday.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة} قال: نصف النهار

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says it was midday, while people were taking their midday rest.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة} قال: نصف النهار والناس قائلون

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r4.claim: Qatada says Moses entered at the midday nap, when people were asleep and least alert.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: دخلها عند القائلة بالظهيرة والناس نائمون وذلك أغفل ما يكون الناس

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through ʿAta al-Khurasani, gives another proposed time: between sunset and the night prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r5.anchor: من طريق ابن جريج عن عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {حين غفلة} قال: ما بين المغرب والعشاء

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports disagreement: some said the time was between sunset and night prayer, others said midday; Ibn Abbas said it was one of those two.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {على حين غفلة} قال: ما بين المغرب والعشاء عن أناس وقال آخرون: نصف النهار وقال ابن عباس: أحدهما

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man from Moses’ own party as an Israelite and the opponent as a Copt; the Copt died from Moses’ blow, which distressed Moses.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته} قال: اسرائيلي {وهذا من عدوه} قال: قبطي

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r8.claim: Mujahid says Moses’ ally was from the Israelites and claims Pharaoh came from Fars, from Istakhr.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته} قال: من قومه من بني إسرائيل وكان فرعون من فارس من اصطخر

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r9.claim: Mujahid says Moses struck the man with his clenched fist.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته}

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r10.claim: Qatada says Moses struck the man with a stick but did not mean to kill him.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {فوكزه موسى} قال: بعصا ولم يتعمد قتله

DURR-FULL:v6p397/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the man Moses struck as Pharaoh’s baker.
DURR-FULL:v6p397/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: الذي وكزه موسى كان خبازا لفرعون

DURR-FULL:v6p398/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p398/r1.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v6p398/r1.claim: Wahb transmits God’s address to Moses: if the slain man had acknowledged God as his creator or provider even once, Moses would have been punished, but God pardoned him because the man never did.
DURR-FULL:v6p398/r1.anchor: عن وهب رضي الله عنه قال: قال الله عز وجل (بعزتي يا ابن عمران لو أن هذه النفس التي وكزت فقتلت اعترفت لي ساعة من ليل أو نهار

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh traveled without Moses; when Moses caught up, he entered Memphis at midday, with markets closed and streets empty, which was the time of heedlessness.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي ان فرعون ركب مركبا ، وليس ، عنده موسى ، فلما جاء موسى قيل له : ان فرعون قد ركب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the time of heedlessness was midday.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة قال : نصف النهار

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Moses entered at midday while people were taking their afternoon rest; similar timing is attributed to Ikrima and al-Suddi.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من اهلها قال : نصف النهار والناس قائلون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r4.claim: Qatada says Moses entered at noon, when people were at their most heedless.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله عز وجل : ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من اهلها قال : دخلها ظهرا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also gives the time as between sunset and the night prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r5.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني ، عن ابن عباس على حين غفلة من اهلها قال : بين المغرب والعشاء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase means a time when people were heedless and not remembering Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن زيد يعني عبد الرحمن على حين غفلة من اهلها قال : على حين غفلة من الناس ، على حين غفلة من ذكر موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says that as Moses grew into manhood, Pharaoh's people could not oppress the Israelites; in the city, Moses saw an Egyptian and an Israelite fighting.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس لما بلغ اشده وكان من الرجال لم يكن أحد من ال فرعون يخلص إلى أحد من بني اسرائيل معه بظلم ولا سخرة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Moses's ally as an Israelite and his enemy as a Copt; similar identifications are attributed to Qatada and al-Suddi.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه ، في قوله : ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من اهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته اسرائيلي وهذا من عدوه قبطي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r2.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets Moses's ally as a Muslim and his enemy as an unbelieving follower of Pharaoh's religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق هذا من شيعته اي مسلم ، وهذا من عدوه ، اي هذا من اهل دين فرعون : كافر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Israelite appealed to Moses for help against the Egyptian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فاستغاثه الاسرائيلي على الفرعوني

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r4.claim: Qatada likewise says the man who sought help was an Israelite appealing to Moses against Pharaoh's enemy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته قال : كان الذي استغاثه رجل من بني اسرائيل استغاث موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses was fiercely angered when the Egyptian assaulted his Israelite ally; Moses struck the Egyptian dead, witnessed only by God and the Israelite.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فغضب موسى غضبا شديدا لانه تناوله وهو يعلم منزلة موسى من بني اسرائيل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r6.claim: Mujahid says Moses struck the Egyptian with the gathered palm of his hand.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد فوكزه موسى بجمع كفه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r7.claim: Qatada says Moses struck the Egyptian with his staff and did not intend to kill him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2954/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فوكزه موسى يقول : فوكزه نبي الله موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعصاه ولم يتعمد قتله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r1.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses was large and strong; angered by the quarrel, he struck the Egyptian dead with one blow without intending to kill him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : وكان موسى قد اوتي بسطة في الخلق ، وشدة في البطش فضب بعدوهما فنازعه ، فوكزه موسى وكزة قتله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the man Moses struck was Pharaoh's baker.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : الذي وكزه موسى كان خبازا لفرعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “he finished him off” to mean the man died, which greatly troubled Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس في وقوله : فقضى عليه فمات ، فكبر ذلك على موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after killing the Egyptian, Moses declared the act to be Satan's work, since Satan is a manifestly misleading enemy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2955/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فقال موسى حين قتل الرجل وهذا من عمل الشيطان انه عدو مضل مبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r1.claim: The story omits many intervening events: Moses grew up in Pharaoh’s palace and was counted among Pharaoh’s household.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r1.anchor: طويت أخبار كثيرة تنبىء عنها القصة وذلك أن موسى يفع وشب في قصر فرعون فكان معدودا من أهل بيت فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r2.claim: One reported account says Moses was called the son of Pharaoh.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r3.claim: The entry into the city continues the episode of God’s instruction to Moses’ mother to nurse him; Moses may have learned his origin from her visits and account of his story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r3.anchor: عطف جزء القصة على جزء آخر منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r4.claim: The city is Memphis, the northern Egyptian capital.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r5.claim: “At a time of heedlessness” attaches grammatically to “entered”; the preposition “on” is metaphorical elevation, like “upon guidance,” meaning he was secure during a heedless interval.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r6.claim: The heedless time was when people rested, dispersed, and left the roads empty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r6.anchor: وهو وقت استراحة الناس وتفرقهم وخلو الطريق منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r7.claim: Some say it was at midday, with Moses crossing the city alone; another report says he was going to catch up with Pharaoh, who had passed through it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r7.anchor: قيل : كان ذلك في وقت القيلولة وكان موسى مجتازا بالمدينة وحده ، قيل ليلحق بفرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r8.claim: Mentioning the hour signals that no one witnessed the Egyptian’s killing, preparing for the accusation in verse 19 and the account of Moses’ departure from Egypt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r8.anchor: الإشارة إلى أن قتله القبطي لم يشعر به أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r9.claim: The two demonstratives unpack the otherwise general statement that two men were fighting.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r10.claim: Arabic demonstratives here need not distinguish near from far: they may match, as here and in 4:143, or differ, as in al-Mutalammis’ poem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r10.anchor: فلذلك قد تكون الإشارتان متماثلتين كما هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r11.claim: A shiʿa is a group affiliated with someone, as in 28:4; an enemy is the group Moses opposed, the Israelites’ adversaries among Pharaoh’s Copts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r12.claim: The man from Moses’ group was an Israelite and his enemy an Egyptian; “enemy” can be grammatically singular or plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p88/r12.anchor: والعدو وصف يستوي فيه الواحد والجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r1.claim: Moses may have known his Israelite identity through his mother’s account of his rescue, and so grew to hate the Copts while inwardly loving the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r1.anchor: أن موسى كان يعلم أنه من بني إسرائيل بإخبار قصة التقاطه من اليم وأن تكون أمه قد أفضت إليه بخبرها وخبره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r2.claim: On either account, Moses’ blow against the Copt was an effort to uphold right; when the later dispute arose, the Copt accused him of tyranny rather than favoritism toward his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r2.anchor: وأما وكزه القبطي فلم يكن إلا انتصارا للحق على جميع التقادير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r3.claim: One report says the Copt worked in Pharaoh’s bakery, asked an Israelite to carry wood to the oven, and tried to force him when he refused, producing a severe fight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r3.anchor: قيل : كان القبطي من عملة مخبز فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r4.claim: “Fighting” is metaphorical here for their severe beating of one another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r4.anchor: فاختصما وتضاربا ضربا شديدا وهو المعبر عنه بالتقاتل على طريق الاستعارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r5.claim: Appealing for help means asking to be rescued from distress or helped against hardship; the call implies the Israelite was overpowered and the Copt unjustly forced labor on him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r5.anchor: فذكر الاستغاثة يؤذن بأن الإسرائيلي كان مغلوبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r6.claim: The Copt was the aggressor because nobody may be compelled to do work against his will.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r6.anchor: وكان ظالما إذ لا يجبر أحد على عمل يعمله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r7.claim: A wakz is a blow with the hand, fingers gathered as in making the form of a seventy-three knot.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r8.claim: This gathering of the fingers is called al-jamʿ, with ḍamma on jīm and sukūn on mīm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r8.anchor: ويسمى الجمع بضم الجيم وسكون الميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r9.claim: “He finished him” is a fixed idiom for death, with an omitted agent understood as death decreeing it; Moses’ blow therefore killed the Copt.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r10.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to God, the only one who decrees death, as in 34:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عائدا إلى الله تعالى المفهوم من المقام إذ لا يقضي بالموت غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r11.claim: Some take the pronoun in “he finished him” to refer to Moses, but Ibn ʿĀshūr says that reading is not evident.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r11.anchor: عائد إلى موسى وليس هذا بالبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r12.claim: Moses did not intend to kill the Egyptian; his blow accidentally struck a vital point and killed him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r12.anchor: وكان هذا قتل خطأ صادف الوكز مقاتل القبطي ولم يرد موسى قتله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r13.claim: The Torah’s Exodus account says Moses looked around, saw no one, killed the Egyptian, and buried him in sand.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p89/r13.anchor: ووقع في سفر الخروج من التوراة في الإصحاح الثاني أن موسى لما رأى المصري يضرب العبراني التفت هنا وهناك ورأى أن ليس أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r1.claim: “He said, this is Satan’s work” is an explanatory resumption answering what Moses did on seeing the Copt die; it shows his immediate concern was religious and is self-directed speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r1.anchor: ماذا كان من أمر موسى حين فوجىء بموت القبطي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r2.claim: “This” may refer to the excessive blow, the death he saw caused by it, or the anger that led to the death.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r3.claim: Satan inflamed Moses’ anger until his blow became excessive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r3.anchor: أن الشيطان أوقد غضبه حتى بالغ في شدة الوكز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r4.claim: Killing a protected person is abhorrent in human laws, since preserving inviolable life is foundational to all religions; Moses may have learned his ancestral religion from his mother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r4.anchor: لأن قتل النفس مستقبح في الشرائع البشرية فإن حفظ النفس المعصومة من أصول الأديان كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r5.claim: Satan’s enmity and routes into human minds explain Moses’ excessive anger: without the satanic thought he would have stopped the Copt, and the killing arose from whispering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r5.anchor: لولا الخاطر الشيطاني لاقتصر على زجر القبطي أو كفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r6.claim: The human soul is originally good and in its natural disposition; deviation from that state requires an external, nonnatural cause such as Satan’s prompting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r6.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن الأصل في النفس الإنسانية هو الخير وأنه الفطرة وأن الانحراف عنها يحتاج إلى سبب غير فطري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r7.claim: The omitted object of Satan’s enmity is Adam and his descendants.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p90/r8.claim: “Manifest” modifies “misleading,” rather than serving as a second or third predicate.

FARRA:v2p303#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p303#2/r2.claim: Wakaza means struck or punched him.

FARRA:v2p303#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v2p303#2/r3.claim: Abdullah reads fa-nakazahu; wahazahu is another Arabic form, and all three verbs mean the same thing.
FARRA:v2p303#2/r3.anchor: قراءة عبد الله (فنكزه) ووهزه أيضا لغة. كل سواء.

FARRA:v2p303#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p303#2/r4.claim: Fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi means that Moses killed him.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r1.claim: The time described as a moment of heedlessness is said to be midday.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r2.claim: The man from Moses' faction was one of his companions, namely an Israelite.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r2.anchor: أي من أصحابه. يعني: بني إسرائيل.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r3.claim: The man's enemy was among Moses' enemies; ʿaduww can refer to one person or a group.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r3.anchor: أي من أعدائه. و "العدو" يدل على الواحد، وعلى الجمع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r4.claim: Wakaza means struck or pushed, like the related verbs lakaza, nakaza, nahaza, and lahaza.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r4.anchor: أي لكزه. يقال وكزته ولكزته [ونكزته ونهزته] ولهزته؛

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r5.claim: Qaḍā ʿalayhi means killed him; qaḍaytu ʿalayhi can mean I finished or settled it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#4/r5.anchor: أي قتله. وكل شيء فرغت منه: فقد قضيته، وقضيت عليه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r16.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r16.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses was attached to Pharaoh, rode with him, and was called Pharaoh’s son; he followed Pharaoh to Memphis and arrived at midday.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r16.anchor: فقال السدي: كان موسى في وقت هذه القصة على رسم التعلق بفرعون وكان يركب مراكبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the city in that account as Memphis and says the time was the midday rest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r17.anchor: فركب فرعون يوما وسار إلى مدينة من مدائن مصر يقال لها منف ثم علم موسى بركوب فرعون فركب بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also identifies the time as the interval between the ʿishāʾ and ʿatama prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r18.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وقال أيضا هو ما بين العشاء والعتمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r19.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r19.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the city was Egypt itself; Moses had openly opposed Pharaoh, was hiding, and entered unrecognized.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r19.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق بل المدينة مصر نفسها، وكان موسى في هذا الوقت قد بدت منه مجاهرة لفرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r20.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r20.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had expelled Moses for years, so they had forgotten each other after the long absence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r20.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: بل كان فرعون قد نابذه وأخرجه من المدينة وغاب عنها سنين فنسي أمره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r21.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r21.claim: Another account says the event happened on a festival day.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r22.claim: “They were fighting” is a circumstantial clause describing the two men as in combat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r22.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يقتتلان في موضع الحال أي مقتتلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r23.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r23.claim: Moses’s faction were the Israelites and his enemy’s faction the Copts.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r24.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r24.claim: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd reports “istaʿānahu” with unmarked ʿayn and nūn, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it a scribal error rather than a reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r24.anchor: وذكر الأخفش سعيد «استعانه» بالعين غير معجمة وبالنون وهي تصحيف لا قراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r25.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r25.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r25.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī identifies Moses’s Israelite ally as al-Sāmirī and the opponent as Pharaoh’s cook.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r25.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي أن الذي من شيعته هو السامري وأن الآخر طباخ فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r26.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r26.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r26.claim: The demonstratives “this one” and “that one” narrate a past scene as if it were presently before the speaker.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r26.anchor: وقوله هذا وهذا حكاية حال قد كانت حاضرة ولذلك عبر ب هذا عن غائب ماض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r27.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r27.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r27.claim: “Wakz” is a blow with the hand clenched into the described formation of seventy-three.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r27.anchor: «والوكز» الضرب باليد مجموعا كعقد ثلاثة وسبعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r28.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r28.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r28.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads “falakazahu”; the meanings are close, but lakz strikes the jaw whereas wakz strikes the torso.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r28.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «فلكزه» والمعنى واحد، إلا أن اللكز في اللحا، والوكز على القلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r29.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r29.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r29.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex also has “fanakazahu,” with the same meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r29.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي أن في مصحف ابن مسعود «فنكزه» بالنون والمعنى واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r30.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r30.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r30.claim: “Qaḍā ʿalayhi” means that Moses killed the man outright.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r31.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r31.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r31.claim: Moses did not intend murder: his blow coincided with the man’s appointed death, and he regretted Satan’s incitement; anger could make his strength exceed his intention.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r31.anchor: وكان موسى عليه السلام لم يرد قتل القبطي لكن وافقت وكزته الأجل وكان عنها موته فندم ورأى أن ذلك من نزغ الشيطان في يده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280#3/r3.speaker: author
