IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280#3/r3.claim: Despite knowing he was forgiven, Moses kept holding himself accountable and will say at the Resurrection that he killed someone without being ordered to.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280#3/r3.anchor: ولم يزل عليه السلام يعتمد ذلك على نفسه مع علمه بأنه قد غفر حتى أنه في القيامة يقول «وقتلت نفسا لم أؤمر بقتلها»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r1.claim: The city Moses entered is identified either as Egypt or as a city near Egypt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r1.anchor: فيها قولان أحدهما أنها مصر والثاني مدينة بالقرب من مصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh rode out while Moses was away; Moses followed after returning, and they reached the city at midday.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r2.anchor: قال السدي ركب فرعون يوما وليس عنده موسى فلما جاء موسى ركب في أثره فأدركه المقيل في تلك المدينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r3.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r3.claim: Another account says Pharaoh suspected Moses was an enemy and expelled him; Moses entered only after growing up, when the people were inattentive.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r3.anchor: وقال غيره لما توهم فرعون في موسى أنه عدوه أمر باخراجه من مدينته فلم يدخل إلا بعد أن كبر فدخلها يوما على حين غفلة من أهلها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r4.speaker: علي عليه السلام
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r4.claim: Ali says the time of heedlessness was a festival when people were occupied with amusement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r4.anchor: أحدها أنه كان يوم عيد لهم وكانوا قد اشتغلوا فيه بلهوهم قاله علي عليه السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by a group and supported by Said ibn Jubayr, says Moses entered at midday.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه دخل نصف النهار رواه جماعة عن ابن عباس وبه قال سعيد ابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r6.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says he entered between sunset and the evening prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r6.anchor: والثالث بين المغرب والعشاء قاله وهب بن منبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the people had forgotten Moses after expelling him, so he entered unnoticed when older.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r7.anchor: والرابع أنهم لما أخرجوه لم يدخل عليهم حتى كبر فدخل على حين غفلة عن ذكره لأنه قد نسي أمره قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r8.claim: Moses' faction means his companions among the Israelites; his enemy's faction means the Copts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r8.anchor: هذا من شيعته أي من أصحابه من بني إسرائيل وهذا من عدوه أي من أعدائه من القبط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says enemy can be singular or plural, and the wording “this one, this one” narrates the scene as if present before a viewer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r9.anchor: والعدو يذكر للواحد وللجمع قال الزجاج وإنما قيل في الغائب هذا وهذا على جهة الحكاية للحضرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r10.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r10.claim: The commentators say the Copt had forced the Israelite to carry wood to Pharaoh's kitchen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r10.anchor: وإن القبطي كان قد سخر الإسرائيلي أن يحمل حطبا إلى مطبخ فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r11.claim: The Israelite's plea for help means that he sought support.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r11.anchor: فاستغاثه أي فاستنصره فوكزه قال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a wakz as striking someone with the whole hand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج الوكز أن يضربه بجميع كفه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r13.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r13.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains wakaz as a blow or shove, using the synonymous verbs wakaza, lakaza, and lahaza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r13.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة فوكزه أي لكزه يقال وكزته ولكزته ولهزته إذا دفعته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r14.claim: “He finished him” means Moses killed him; the expression also describes finishing a task.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r14.anchor: فقضى عليه أي قتله وكل شئ فرغت منه فقد قضيته وقضيت عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r15.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r15.claim: Mujahid says Moses struck the man with his palm.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r16.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r16.claim: Qatada says Moses struck the man with his staff.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r17.claim: Moses regretted the death because he had not intended to kill the Copt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r17.anchor: فلما مات القبطي ندم موسى لأنه لم يرد قتله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r18.claim: By calling it Satan's work, Moses means Satan stirred his anger until he struck the man.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r18.anchor: أي هو الذي هيج غضبي حتى ضربت هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r19.claim: Satan is an evident enemy and misleader of Adam's descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207#2/r19.anchor: إنه عدو لابن آدم مضل له مبين عداوته

MAJAZ:v2p99/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r5.claim: Wakaza means he struck him in the chest with his clenched fist; it is a kind of lakz or lahz.
MAJAZ:v2p99/r5.anchor: بمنزلة لهزه فى صدره بجمع كفه، فهو اللكز واللهز

MAJAZ:v2p99/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r6.claim: Qaḍā ʿalayhi means he killed him and finished him off.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.claim: The killing of the Egyptian led, within God's decree, to Moses leaving Egypt for Midian and the prophethood and discourse destined for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.anchor: قضية قتله ذلك القبطي، الذي كان سبب خروجه من الديار المصرية إلى بلاد مدين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses entered the city between sunset and nightfall.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: وذلك بين المغرب والعشاء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة، السدي، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.claim: These authorities say Moses entered the city at midday.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: كان ذلك نصف النهار. وكذلك قال سعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، والسدي، وقتادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، السدي، محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.claim: The man from Moses's party was an Israelite and the opponent from his enemies was an Egyptian Copt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.anchor: أي: من بني إسرائيل (1) ، {وهذا من عدوه} أي: قبطي، قاله ابن عباس، وقتادة، والسدي، ومحمد بن إسحاق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.claim: The Israelite appealed to Moses, who found an opportunity while people were unaware and struck the Egyptian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.anchor: فاستغاث الإسرائيلي بموسى، عليه السلام، ووجد موسى فرصة، وهي غفلة الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says Moses struck the Egyptian with the gathered fist of his hand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد: وكزه، أي: طعنه بجمع (2) كفه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r9.claim: Qatada says Moses struck him with a staff he had with him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: وكزه بعصا كانت معه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225/r1.claim: The blow proved fatal and the Egyptian died.

JISHUMI:v8p5478/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r4.claim: Wakz can mean pushing, striking with a closed hand, or stabbing; nakaza and lahaza are comparable verbs.
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r4.anchor: والوكز: الدفع، والوكز: الضرب بجمع الكف، والوكز: الطعن

JISHUMI:v8p5483/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r1.claim: The killing was not created by God, refuting the determinists: if God created it and the devil prompted it, attribution to the latter would be more fitting.
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r1.anchor: أنه لم يكن خلقا لله تعالى فيبطل قول المجبرة؛ لأنه لو خلق فيه ذلك

JISHUMI:v8p5483/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r2.claim: The description of Satan as a misleader shows God does not mislead: if misguidance were God's creation, Satan would not be called a misleader.
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r2.anchor: أن الضلال لو كان خلقا له لما كان الشيطان مضلا

JISHUMI:v8p5483/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r3.claim: A second argument is that God censures Satan as a misleader, so God cannot himself mislead.
JISHUMI:v8p5483/r3.anchor: أنه ذم الشيطان بأنه مضل فكيف يضل هو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r1.claim: The city was Egypt, or specifically Memphis in Egypt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r1.anchor: المدينة : مصر . وقيل : مدينة منف من أرض مصر .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r2.claim: The time of heedlessness may have been between the evening prayers, the midday nap, or a festival when people were occupied with entertainment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r2.anchor: وحين غفلتهم : ما بين العشاءين . وقيل : وقت القائلة . وقيل : يوم عيد لهم هم مشتغلون فيه بلهوهم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r3.claim: Another account says that after Moses grew up, spoke truth, and denounced the Egyptians, they frightened him, so he entered towns only when their people were unaware.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : لما شب وعقل أخذ يتكلم بالحق وينكر عليهم ، فأخافوه ، فلا يدخل قرية إلا على تغفل .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh reads فاستعانه, 'he sought his aid.'

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r5.claim: Moses' supporter was from the Israelites who followed his religion; an alternative identifies him as the Samaritan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r5.anchor: { من شيعته } ممن شايعه على دينه من بني إسرائيل . وقيل : هو السامري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.claim: Moses' adversary was an opposing Copt named Fātūn, who was forcing an Israelite to carry wood to Pharaoh's kitchen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.anchor: { من عدوه } من مخالفيه من القبط ، وهو فاتون ، وكان يتسخر الإسرائيلي لحمل الحطب إلى مطبخ فرعون .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.claim: A wakz is a push with the fingertips; another explanation says it is a blow with the whole fist.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.anchor: والوكز : الدفع بأطراف الأصابع . وقيل : بجمع الكف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the verb as فلكزه, with lām.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r9.claim: فقضى عليه means that Moses killed the man.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r10.claim: Moses called the killing Satan's work and sought forgiveness because he killed before receiving permission; this made it a sin requiring repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r10.anchor: لأنه قتله قبل أن يؤذن له في القتل ، فكان ذنبا يستغفر منه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a prophet may not kill unless commanded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن جريج : ليس لنبي أن يقتل ما لم يؤمر

NAHHAS:v3p231/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p231/r7.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn ʿAbbās, say Moses entered the city at midday.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r7.anchor: أكثر أهل التفسير منهم ابن عباس على أنه دخل نصف النهار

NAHHAS:v3p231/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r8.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p231/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Moses deliberately sought the city when its inhabitants were inattentive, entering when he knew this; he killed the man before being commanded to do so, then sought forgiveness and was forgiven.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك طلب أن يدخل المدينة وقت غفلة أهلها فدخلها حين علم منهم ذلك فكان منه ما كان من قتل الرجل من قبل أن يؤمر بقتله

NAHHAS:v3p231/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p231/r9.claim: Ordinary speech says ‘I entered the city when its people were heedless,’ not ‘upon a time when its people were heedless’; the verse uses ʿalā because the heedlessness itself is intended, like ‘I came upon heedlessness’ or ‘upon a time of heedlessness.’
NAHHAS:v3p231/r9.anchor: ويقال في الكلام دخلت المدينة حين غفل أهلها ولا يقال على حين غفل أهلها ودخلت على في هذه الآية لأن الغفلة هي المقصودة

NAHHAS:v3p231/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p231/r10.claim: The clause ‘this is from his faction’ is a subject and predicate; a viewer identifies one man as an Israelite and the other as one of Pharaoh’s people. ʿAduw can mean enemies and can remain unchanged for feminine or plural.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r10.anchor: ( فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته ) ابتداء وخبر

NAHHAS:v3p231/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r11.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v3p231/r11.claim: The Basrans allow a feminine tāʾ in ʿaduww because it means ‘hostile’; the Kufans attribute the untāʾ form to a weak wāw, which al-Naḥḥās rejects because wāw is a strong consonant.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r11.anchor: ومن العرب من يدخل الهاء في المؤنث لأنه بمعنى معادية عند البصريين وعند الكوفيين لأن الواو خفية

NAHHAS:v3p231/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p231/r12.claim: ‘An enemy, a clear misleader’ can be parsed as two successive predicates or as adjectives.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r12.anchor: ( إنه عدو مضل مبين ) خبر بعد خبر وإن شئت كان مضل مبين نعتا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r21.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r21.claim: Ibn Shajara identifies the city Moses entered as Egypt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r21.anchor: أحدها : أنها مصر , قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r22.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r22.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the city as Memphis.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r23.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r23.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the city as Heliopolis.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r24.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r24.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the city’s people were napping at midday.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r24.anchor: أحدها : نصف النهار والناس قائلون , قاله ابن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r25.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r25.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it was between sunset and nightfall.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r25.anchor: الثاني : ما بين المغرب والعشاء , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r26.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r26.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it was a festival day when people were occupied in amusement.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r26.anchor: الثالث : يوم عيد لهم وهم في لهوهم , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r27.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r27.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says they were heedless because a long absence had made them forget Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r27.anchor: الرابع : لأنهم غفلوا عن ذكره لبعد عهدهم به , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r28.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r28.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the man from Moses’s faction was an Israelite and his enemy was an Egyptian Copt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r28.anchor: أحدهما : من شيعته إسرائيلي ومن عدوه قبطي ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r29.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r29.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the man from Moses’s faction was a Muslim and his enemy an unbeliever.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r29.anchor: الثاني : من شيعته مسلم ومن عدوه كافر ، قاله ابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r30.speaker: ابن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r30.claim: Ibn Sallām relates that a Copt ordered an Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh’s kitchen; when he refused, he appealed to Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r30.anchor: حكى ابن سلام أن القبطي سخر الإسرائيلي ليحمل له حطبا لمطبخ فرعون فأبى عليه فاستغاث بموسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r31.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r31.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Copt was Pharaoh’s baker.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r31.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : وكان خبازا لفرعون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r32.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r32.claim: Qatāda says Moses struck the man with his staff.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r33.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r33.claim: Mujāhid says Moses struck him with his palm, meaning he pushed him; wakz and lakz both mean pushing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r33.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بكفه أي دفعه , الوكز واللكز واحد والدفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r1.speaker: رؤبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r1.claim: Ruʾba’s line is cited for the word wakz.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r2.claim: Wakz is a strike to the chest, whereas lakz is a strike to the back.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r2.anchor: إلا أن الوكز في الصدر واللكز في الظهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r3.claim: Moses meant to push the man away, not kill him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r3.anchor: فعل موسى ذلك وهو لا يريد قتله وانما يريد دفعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r4.claim: Fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi means Moses killed him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r5.claim: Calling it Satan’s work means it came from Satan’s enticement.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r5.anchor: قال هذا من عمل الشيطان } أي من إغوائه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says killing an unbeliever was not lawful then because fighting was being restrained.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : لم يكن يحل قتل الكافر يومئذ في تلك الحال لأنها كانت حال كف عن القتال

MUJAHID:v2p482/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p482/r1.claim: The man from Moses's party was one of the Israelites; Pharaoh was Persian and came from Istakhr.
MUJAHID:v2p482/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته ﴾ قال يعني من قومه بني إسرائيل قال وكان فرعون من فارس من اصطخر

MUJAHID:v2p482/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p482/r2.claim: Moses struck the man with a closed fist.
MUJAHID:v2p482/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فوكزه موسى ﴾ قال يعني بجمع كفه

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.claim: Moses was at a village called Khanin, two farsakhs away, and came to the town at midday.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.anchor: وكان بقرية تدعى خانين على رأس فرسخين، فأتى المدينة فدخلها نصف النهار.

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r4.claim: The city means the village, and the time of people’s unawareness was midday, during the siesta.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r4.anchor: يعني القرية { على حين غفلة من أهلها } يعني نصف النهار، وقت القائلة،

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r5.claim: The two men were unbelievers: one was from Moses’ people, the Israelites, and the other was his enemy, an Egyptian Copt.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r5.anchor: كافرين { يقتتلان هذا من شيعته } يعني هذا من جنس موسى، من بني إسرائيل { وهذا } الآخر { من عدوه } من القبط،

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r6.claim: The Israelite appealed to Moses for help against the Egyptian; Moses struck him once with his hand and killed him, since Moses was very strong.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r6.anchor: فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى } بكفه مرة واحدة، { فقضى عليه } الموت،

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r7.claim: Moses regretted the killing, saying he had not been commanded to kill; Satan had made the act seem good to him and is a clear misleader.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r7.anchor: ثم ندم موسى، عليه السلام، فقال: إني لم أومر بالقتل، { قال هذا من عمل الشيطان } يعني من تزيين الشيطان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r1.claim: The city Moses entered is Egypt.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r2.claim: The time when its people were unaware is said to be either between the evening prayers or at the midday siesta.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r2.anchor: وهو ما بين العشاءين أو وقت الفائلة يعني انتصاف النهار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r3.claim: Another explanation is that, after growing up, Moses spoke truth and denounced them, so they frightened him and he entered only when people were inattentive.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r3.anchor: وقيل لما شب وعقل أخذ يتكلم بالحق وينكر عليهم فأخافوه فلا يدخل المدينة إلا على تغفل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r4.claim: Moses’s faction member was among his Israelite coreligionists; شيعة means followers and supporters.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r4.anchor: ممن شايعه على دينه من بني أسرائيل قيل هو السامري وشيعة الرجل أتباعه وأنصاره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r5.claim: One report identifies the man from Moses’s faction as the Samaritan.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r6.claim: The man from the enemy group was an Egyptian, identified as Fāton; calling them this and that can narrate as if they were present.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r6.anchor: من مخالفيه من القبط وهو فاتون وقيل فيهما هذا وهذا وإن كانا غائبين على جهة الحكاية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r7.claim: The faction member sought Moses’s help against the enemy; استغاثه means he asked him for support.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r8.claim: وكزه means striking with the gathered fist or with the tips of the fingers.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r8.anchor: ضربه بجمع كفه أو بأطراف أصابعه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r9.claim: Moses killed the man, but the killing was unintentional.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى القتل الحاصل بغير قصد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r10.claim: Moses called it Satan’s work and wronging himself because he had protected status among them, so killing the protected enemy combatant was unlawful, or because he acted before permission.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r10.anchor: وإنما جعل قتل الكافر من عمل الشيطان وسماه ظلما لنفسه واستغفر منه لأنه كان مستأمنا فيهم ولا يحل قتل الكافر الحربي المستأمن أو لأنه قتله قبل أن يؤذن له في القتل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r11.speaker: ابن جريح
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a prophet may not kill unless he has been commanded to do so.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p230/r11.anchor: وعن ابن جريح ليس لنبي أن يقتل ما لم يؤمر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r1.claim: One chronology says Moses had learned the truth of his faith and openly criticized Pharaoh's people, who frightened him, so he entered the city secretly.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r1.anchor: قيل: لما عرف موسى عليه السلام ما هو عليه من الحق في دينه، عاب ما عليه قوم فرعون وفشا ذلك منه فأخافوه فخافهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses still lived in Pharaoh's orbit, rode his mounts, and was called Pharaoh's son; he followed Pharaoh to a town called Menf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: كان موسى في وقت هذه القصة على رسم التعلق بفرعون، وكان يركب مراكبه، حتى كان يدعى موسى ابن فرعون فركب فرعون يوما وسار إلى مدينة من مدائن مصر يقال لها منف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r3.claim: Maqatil locates Menf two parasangs from Egypt.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل على رأس فرسخين من مصر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the time of negligence as the midday rest, and also as between the evening prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r4.anchor: في وقت القائلة، وهو وقت الغفلة قاله ابن عباس. وقال أيضا: هو بين العشاء والعتمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the city was Egypt itself and Moses had openly opposed Pharaoh and criticized their worship of Pharaoh and idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r5.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: بل المدينة مصر نفسها، وكان موسى في هذا الوقت قد أظهر خلاف فرعون، وعاب عليهم عبادة فرعون والأصنام،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatada say the neglected time was midday while people slept.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة: وقت الظهيرة والناس نيام.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had expelled Moses for years; Moses returned when people had forgotten him, on a festival day.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: كان فرعون قد نابذ موسى وأخرجه من المدينة، وغاب عنها سنين، وجاء والناس على غفلة بنسيانهم لأمره، وبعد عهدهم به، وكان ذلك يوم عيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says Moses deliberately entered when he knew residents were heedless; he killed the man before being commanded to do so and then sought and received forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: طلب أن يدخل المدينة وقت غفلة أهلها، فدخلها حين علم ذلك منهم، فكان منه من قتل الرجل من قبل أن يؤمر بقتله، فاستغفر ربه فغفر له.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r9.claim: The preposition على is used because heedlessness is the point: Arabic permits both 'I came at a moment of heedlessness' and 'at a time of heedlessness.'
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r9.anchor: فدخلت { على } في هذه الآية لأن الغفلة هي المقصودة فصار هذا كما تقول: جئت على غفلة، وإن شئت قلت: جئت على حين غفلة،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r10.claim: The onlooker would identify the man from Moses's faction as an Israelite and the enemy as one of Pharaoh's people.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r10.anchor: والمعنى إذا نظر إليهما الناظر قال هذا من شيعته أي من بني إسرائيل { وهذا من عدوه } أي من قوم فرعون.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r11.claim: The Israelite asked Moses for aid; Qurtubi also reads the following day's appeal as a plea for help against another Egyptian.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r11.anchor: أي طلب نصره وغوثه، وكذا قال في الآية بعدها: { فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه } أي يستغيث به على قبطي آخر.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r12.claim: Helping the oppressed is a religious duty among all communities and in every revealed law.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r12.anchor: وإنما أغاثه لأن نصر المظلوم دين في الملل كلها على الأمم، وفرض في جميع الشرائع.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r13.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r13.claim: Qatada says the Egyptian tried to force the Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh's kitchen; the Israelite refused and called for Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: أراد القبطي أن يسخر الإسرائيلي ليحمل حطبا لمطبخ فرعون فأبى عليه، فاستغاث بموسى.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the Israelite was Pharaoh's baker.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r14.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: وكان خبازا لفرعون.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r15.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r15.claim: Qatada says Moses struck the man with his staff; Mujahid says he used his hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r15.anchor: قال قتادة: بعصاه. وقال مجاهد: بكفه أي دفعه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r16.claim: Wakz, lakz, lahz, and lahd mean striking with a fist formed by curling the hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r16.anchor: والوكز واللكز واللهز واللهد بمعنى واحد، وهو الضرب بجمع الكف مجموعا كعقد ثلاثة وسبعين.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r17.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has لكزه; one distinction says lakz is a blow to the jaw and wakz to the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: { فلكزه }. وقيل: اللكز في اللحى والوكز على القلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r18.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r18.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says Ibn Masud's codex had the variant فنكزه, with the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r18.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي أن في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود «فنكزه» بالنون والمعنى واحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r19.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r19.claim: Al-Jawhari quotes Abu Ubayda defining lakz as a fist blow to the chest.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15/r19.anchor: وقال الجوهري عن أبي عبيدة: اللكز الضرب بالجمع على الصدر.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r1.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r1.claim: Abu Zayd says the blow reaches throughout the body.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: في جميع الجسد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r2.claim: Al-wahlaz is striking the chest with the gathered hand, like al-lakz.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r2.anchor: واللهز: الضرب بجمع اليد في الصدر مثل اللكز عن أبي عبيدة أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r3.claim: A person struck with the gathered hand at the jaw, neck, or leg is called malhaz, with a kasra on its mīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: هو بالجمع في اللهازم والرقبة والرجل ملهز بكسر الميم.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r4.claim: Nakazahu means he struck and pushed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r4.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: نكزه أي ضربه ودفعه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r5.claim: Nahazahu, like nakazahu and wakazahu, means he struck and pushed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r5.anchor: الكسائي: نهزه مثل نكزه ووكزه، أي ضربه ودفعه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r6.claim: Lahadahu means he pushed him down in humiliation; the person pushed is malhūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r6.anchor: ولهده لهدا أي دفعه لذله فهو ملهود

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r7.speaker: طرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r7.claim: Tarafa uses malhad in an insulting poem to mean someone who is pushed about.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r7.anchor: قال طرفة يذم رجلا: بطيء عن الداعي سريع إلى الخنا ذلول بأجماع الرجال ملهد أي مدفع

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r8.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r8.claim: Aisha says the Prophet gave her a painful push; Muslim transmitted the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r8.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: فلهدني تعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لهدة أوجعني خرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r9.claim: Moses did not intend to kill the man; he meant only to push him away, but the blow caused his death.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r9.anchor: ففعل موسى عليه السلام ذلك وهو لا يريد قتله، إنما قصد دفعه فكانت فيه نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r10.claim: The phrase qada alayhi means he finished him off; more generally it means completing something one has undertaken.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r10.anchor: وهو معنى: { فقضى عليه }. وكل شيء أتيت عليه وفرغت منه قضيت عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r11.speaker: الأشجع
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15#2/r11.claim: A verse attributed to al-Ashjaʿ uses qada alayhi for killing or finishing someone.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r1.claim: Calling the killing Satan's work means it came from Satan's misguidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r1.anchor: { قال هذا من عمل الشيطان } أي من إغوائه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r2.claim: Hasan says killing an unbeliever was not permitted then, since fighting had been suspended.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: لم يكن يحل قتل الكافر يومئذ في تلك الحال لأنها كانت حال كف عن القتال.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r3.claim: The description of Satan as an evident enemy is a second predicate following the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r3.anchor: { إنه عدو مضل مبين } خبر بعد خبر.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r9.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r9.claim: Kaʿb says Moses was twelve years old and the killing was accidental, since a blow or push usually does not kill.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:15-16/r9.anchor: وقال كعب: كان إذ ذاك ابن اثنتي عشرة سنة، وكان قتله مع ذلك خطأ فإن الوكزة واللكزة في الغالب لا تقتل.

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.claim: The waw in ‘and he entered the city’ does not establish sequence, so this reading cannot date Moses’ prophethood relative to the killing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.anchor: لأن الواو في قوله : { ودخل المدينة } لا تفيد الترتيب

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.claim: The passage indicates that God favored Moses with wisdom and knowledge before the killing of the Copt.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.anchor: ثم بين إنعامه عليه قبل قتل القبطي

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r8.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r8.claim: The city was the place where Pharaoh lived, a town about two farsakhs from Egypt.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r8.anchor: فالجمهور على أنها هي المدينة التي كان يسكنها فرعون ، وهي قرية على رأس فرسخين من مصر

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r9.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the city as ʿAyn Shams.

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r10.speaker: القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r10.claim: The first account says Moses publicly condemned Pharaoh’s false religion, became feared, and entered while the inhabitants were heedless.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r10.anchor: القول الأول : أن موسى عليه السلام لما بلغ أشده واستوى وآتاه الله الحكم والعلم في دينه ودين آبائه ، علم أن فرعون وقومه على الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r11.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r11.claim: Most say Moses entered at midday, when the people were taking their siesta.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r11.anchor: ثم الأكثرون على أنه عليه السلام دخلها نصف النهار وقت ما هم قائلون

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās places Moses’ entry between sunset and the evening prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس يريد بين المغرب والعشاء

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r13.claim: Rāzī prefers the midday account: the verse attributes heedlessness to the inhabitants, which fear-driven secret entry alone would not explain.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r13.anchor: والأول أولى ، لأنه تعالى أضاف الغفلة إلى أهلها ، وإذا دخل المرء مستترا لأجل خوف ، لا تضاف الغفلة إلى القوم

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r14.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r14.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses dressed and rode like Pharaoh and was called Pharaoh’s son; he entered at midday when the roads were empty.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r14.anchor: قال السدي : إن موسى عليه السلام حين كبر كان يركب مراكب فرعون ، ويلبس مثل ما يلبس ، ويدعى موسى ابن فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r15.claim: Ibn Zayd reads ‘heedlessness’ as forgetting Moses: after an infant incident that caused his speech impediment, Pharaoh banished him, and the people later forgot him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r15.anchor: قال ابن زيد : ليس المراد من قوله : { على حين غفلة من أهلها } حصول الغفلة في تلك الساعة ، بل المراد الغفلة من ذكر موسى وأمره

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r16.claim: Rāzī says none of these reports can be preferred over the others because the Qur’an gives no evidence for any of them.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r16.anchor: ولا مطمع في ترجيح بعض هذه الروايات على بعض ، لأنه ليس في القرآن ما يدل على شيء منها

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the two demonstratives as narrated speech: a viewer would say ‘this one is from his faction and this one from his enemy.’
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : قال : هذا وهذا وهما غائبان على وجه الحكاية

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r2.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r2.claim: Muqātil says both fighters were unbelievers, one Israelite and one Copt, citing Moses’ next-day rebuke that the man was plainly misguided.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r2.anchor: فقال مقاتل : الرجلان كانا كافرين ، إلا أن أحدهما من بني إسرائيل ، والآخر من القبط ، واحتج عليه بأن موسى عليه السلام قال له في اليوم الثاني { إنك لغوى مبين }

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r3.claim: The well-known view is that Moses’ factional ally was Muslim, since someone who differs in religion and way is not ordinarily called one’s partisan.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r3.anchor: والمشهور أن الذي من شيعته كان مسلما ، لأنه لا يقال فيمن يخالف الرجل في دينه وطريقه : إنه من شيعته

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r4.claim: Some say the Copt who bullied the Israelite was Pharaoh’s cook and had forced him to carry firewood to the kitchen.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r4.anchor: وقيل إن القبطي الذي سخر الإسرائيلي كان

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r5.claim: Another account identifies the two fighters as the Samaritan, who belonged to Moses’ faction, and Pharaoh’s cook.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r5.anchor: وقيل الرجلان المقتتلان : أحدهما السامري وهو الذي من شيعته ، والآخر طباخ فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r6.claim: The factional ally’s appeal means he asked Moses to rescue him and sought his support against the Copt.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r6.anchor: أي سأله أن يخلصه منه واستنصره عليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r7.claim: Wakz means pushing with the fingertips.

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r8.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r8.claim: An alternative lexical explanation says wakz is a push with the closed hand.

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading has ‘Moses struck him’ using the verb lakaza instead of wakaza.

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r10.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r10.claim: Some distinguish the verbs by saying wakz is to the chest and lakz to the back.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الوكز في الصدر واللكز في الظهر

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r12.claim: Some exegetes say Moses struck the man with his staff; al-Mufaḍḍal rejects this as erroneous because the verb is not used for striking with a staff.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r12.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : فوكزه بعصاه ، قال المفضل هذا غلط ، لأنه لا يقال وكزه بالعصا

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r13.claim: The phrase ‘he finished him’ means that Moses killed him.

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r14.speaker: من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r14.claim: Critics argue that if the Copt deserved death, Moses’ Satan attribution, plea for forgiveness, and confession of error are puzzling; if not, killing him was sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r14.anchor: احتج بهذه الآية من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء عليه السلام من وجوه : أحدها : أن ذلك القبطي إما أن يقال إنه كان مستحق القتل

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r15.speaker: من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r15.claim: They argue that calling the Copt an enemy implies a belligerent unbeliever whose blood was lawful, so asking forgiveness wrongly suggests a permissible act was forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r15.anchor: وثانيها : أن قوله : { وهاذا من عدوه } يدل على أنه كان كافرا حربيا فكان دمه مباحا فلم استغفر عنه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r16.speaker: من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r16.claim: They argue that a push is not normally intended to kill, making the death accidental and Moses’ plea for forgiveness inexplicable.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200/r16.anchor: وثالثها : أن الوكز لا يقصد به القتل ظاهرا ، فكان ذلك القتل قتل خطأ ، فلم استغفر منه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r1.claim: One reading says God permitted killing the unbeliever but preferred postponement; Moses’ act of leaving that recommendation was the Satanic deed.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r1.anchor: لعل الله تعالى وإن أباح قتل الكافر إلا أنه قال الأولى تأخير قتلهم إلى زمان آخر

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r2.claim: A second reading makes ‘this’ point to the slain man’s conduct: his action was Satanic and made him an opponent of God deserving death.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r2.anchor: أن قوله ( هذا ) إشارة إلى عمل المقتول لا إلى عمل نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r3.claim: A third reading makes ‘this’ point to the slain man himself as one of Satan’s faction; the idiom means belonging to Satan’s party.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون قوله ( هذا ) إشارة إلى المقتول ، يعني أنه من جند الشيطان وحزبه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r9.claim: In ‘I was among the astray,’ Moses does not admit religious error; he denies Pharaoh’s claim that he was an unbeliever and admits confusion about what action was required.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r9.anchor: لم يقل إني صرت بذلك ضالا ، ولكن فرعون لما

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r10.claim: Whether an unbeliever’s blood is lawful varies between religious laws; perhaps killing the Copt was prohibited under Moses’ law.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r10.anchor: كون الكافر مباح الدم أمر يختلف باختلاف الشرائع فلعل قتلهم كان حراما في ذلك الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r11.claim: Even if the killing was permitted, Moses may have sought forgiveness because refraining from it would have been preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r11.anchor: أو إن كان مباحا لكن الأولى تركه على ما قررنا

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r12.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that the killing was accidental: the man may have been weak while Moses was extremely strong, so the blow certainly killed him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r12.anchor: قلنا لا نسلم فلعل الرجل كان ضعيفا وموسى عليه السلام كان في نهاية الشدة ، فوكزه كان قاتلا قطعا

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r13.claim: Even if the death was accidental, Moses could have freed the Israelite without delivering the fatal blow, so he sought forgiveness for choosing the worse course.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r13.anchor: ولكن لعله عليه السلام كان يمكنه أن يخلص الإسرائيلي من يده بدون ذلك الوكز الذي كان الأولى تركه

RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r14.claim: Even if the verse proves a sin, it does not establish that Moses was already a messenger; the act could have preceded prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v24p200#2/r14.anchor: لكنا بينا أنه لا دليل ألبتة على أنه كان رسولا في ذلك الوقت فيكون ذلك صادرا منه قبل النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that because Moses calls the act Satan’s work, it cannot be created by God; they compare Joseph, Moses’ companion, and the expulsion of Adam’s parents.
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r1.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الآية دلت على بطلان قول من نسب المعاصي إلى الله تعالى لأنه عليه السلام قال : { هاذا من عمل الشيطان }

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r1.claim: R identifies the city as the capital where Pharaoh resided.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r1.anchor: thought to be the capital city in which Pharaoh resided (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r2.claim: R also names Heliopolis as a possible location for the city.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r2.anchor: some specify that it was Heliopolis (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r3.claim: Ṭ names Memphis as another possible location.

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r4.claim: The source of these location identifications is unclear; the commentary compares Exodus 2:11–15.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r4.anchor: it is unclear where this information originates (cf. Exodus 2:11–15)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r5.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r5.claim: Q and Ṭ understand the time of heedlessness as midday, when most inhabitants were asleep.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r5.anchor: a time when most of the inhabitants were asleep at midday (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r6.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r6.claim: Most commentators say Moses was identifiable as part of Pharaoh's retinue and was called Pharaoh's son by then.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r6.anchor: was even called“the son of Pharaoh” (Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r7.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r7.claim: R reports another view that Moses had already opposed Pharaoh and been cast out by then.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r7.anchor: Others say that by this time Moses had already shown his opposition to Pharaoh and had been cast out (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r8.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r8.claim: Q and Ṭ also read heedlessness as the people no longer knowing or remembering Moses.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r8.anchor: heedlessness refers to the fact that the people did not know or remember Moses anymore (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r9.claim: R identifies Moses' faction as the Israelites and his enemies as the Egyptians.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r9.anchor: His own faction refers to the Israelites, and his enemies, the Egyptians (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r10.speaker: M
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r10.claim: M speculates that the adversary may have been another Israelite who disbelieved and was therefore an enemy.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r10.anchor: the adversary mentioned in this verse could have been another Israelite, but one who was a disbeliever and thus an enemy (M)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r11.claim: The Biblical account explicitly says the first adversary was Egyptian (Exodus 2:12).
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r11.anchor: The Biblical story mentions explicitly that it was an Egyptian (Exodus 2:12)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r12.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r12.claim: Some Muslim commentators follow the Biblical account in identifying this verse's adversary as Egyptian.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r12.anchor: some Muslim commentators rely on the Biblical account in also identifying the adversary in this verse as Egyptian

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r13.claim: The different wording in 28:19 could imply that the second opponent was an enemy through disbelief, not necessarily another Egyptian.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r13.anchor: could suggest, if one accepts the interpretation that enmity can also be a matter of whether one is a disbeliever

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r14.claim: The commentary also notes that 28:15 calls Satan an enemy.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r14.anchor: it can also be noted that v. 15 also mentions Satan as an enemy

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r15.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r15.claim: The wording implies Moses did not intend to kill the Egyptian and struck only to defend the Israelite.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r15.anchor: Moses did not intend to kill the Egyptian, but only to defend the Israelite (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r16.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r16.claim: Q says killing was inappropriate for a prophet; the sin was striking the man so forcefully that he died, not murder itself.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r16.anchor: the sin was not murder, but striking him in such a manner as to result in his death (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:15/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r17.claim: Commentators generally avoid attributing sin to Moses or any prophet.
STUDYQURAN:28:15/r17.anchor: In general commentators are careful, here and elsewhere, to keep from attributing sin to Moses or any prophet

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r1.claim: The city is Memphis in Egypt, and the time of entry was the midday nap.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r1.anchor: {المدينة} [الأعراف: 123] مدينة منف من مصر {على حين غفلة من أهلها} [القصص: 15] وذلك عند القائلة نصف النهار

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses pursued Pharaoh after missing his departure, caught up during Pharaoh’s midday rest at Memphis, and entered when markets and streets were deserted.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " كان موسى حين كبر يركب مراكب فرعون، ويلبس مثل ما يلبس، وكان إنما يدعى موسى بن فرعون

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses had Israelite followers, recognized Pharaoh’s religion as false, publicly opposed it, and entered Pharaoh’s town secretly because both sides feared each other.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: «لما بلغ موسى أشده واستوى، آتاه الله حكما وعلما، فكانت له من بني إسرائيل شيعة يسمعون منه ويطيعونه ويجتمعون إليه

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Pharaoh had expelled Moses after he struck him with a staff as a child; Moses returned only after growing up, so the lapse was forgetfulness of his affair, not an hour of the day.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {على حين غفلة من أهلها} [القصص: 15] قال: ليس غفلة من ساعة، ولكن غفلة من ذكر موسى وأمره

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd’s report says Pharaoh’s wife argued that the child was small, gave him embers, and Moses put a coal in his mouth, causing the speech knot later mentioned in the prayer for eloquence.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {على حين غفلة من أهلها} [القصص: 15] قال: ليس غفلة من ساعة، ولكن غفلة من ذكر موسى وأمره

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī declines to decide why Moses entered then, retaining the Qur’anic wording that he entered when the people were unaware.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في الصحة بذلك أن يقال كما قال الله جل ثناؤه: {ولما بلغ أشده واستوى} [القصص: 14] {ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها} [القصص: 15]

TAB-FULL:v18p183/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r7.speaker: some interpreters
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r7.claim: One reported view identifies the time of the people’s unawareness as midday.
TAB-FULL:v18p183/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في الوقت الذي عني بقوله: {على حين غفلة من أهلها} [القصص: 15] فقال بعضهم: ذلك نصف النهار

TAB-FULL:v18p185/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the time as midday.
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها}

TAB-FULL:v18p185/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r2.claim: A report through ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says people placed the event at the midday nap, while Ibn ʿAbbās said it was between sunset and nightfall.
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r2.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني، عن ابن عباس، قال: " يقولون في القائلة

TAB-FULL:v18p185/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r3.claim: Qatada says Moses entered after reaching maturity, at the midday nap.
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها}

TAB-FULL:v18p185/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p185/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses entered at midday.

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r1.claim: The verb وَكَزَ means that Moses struck the man with the gathered fist of his hand.

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that a Copt was forcing a Muslim to work; after the Israelite appealed and Moses ordered the Copt to release him, Moses struck and killed the Copt in anger.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " أساء موسى من حيث أساء، وهو شديد الغضب شديد القوة، فمر برجل من القبط قد تسخر رجلا من المسلمين

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.claim: In another report, the Israelite later appealed while fighting another man; the man recognized Moses as the killer from the previous day, and the news led to Moses fleeing.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: " {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان} [القصص: 15] قال: رجل من بني إسرائيل يقاتل جبارا لفرعون فاستغاثه

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the ally as an Israelite and the enemy as a Copt from Pharaoh’s household.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، " {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان، هذا من شيعته، وهذا من عدوه} [القصص: 15] أما الذي من شيعته فمن بني إسرائيل

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r5.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the enemy as one of the Copts and repeats that the Israelite appealed to Moses against him.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r5.anchor: عن السدي، " {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان، هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه} [القصص: 15] يقول: من القبط

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses had prevented Pharaoh’s household from oppressing Israelites; an Israelite appealed to him against a man of Pharaoh’s family, and Moses killed the man in anger, witnessed only by God and the Israelite.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما بلغ موسى أشده، وكان من الرجال، لم يكن أحد من آل فرعون يخلص إلى أحد من بني إسرائيل معه بظلم ولا سخرة

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq calls the ally a Muslim and the opponent an unbeliever of Pharaoh’s religion; Moses was large and powerful, and killed the opponent with a blow without intending to kill him.
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان، هذا من شيعته} [القصص: 15] مسلم، وهذا من أهل دين فرعون كافر

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses’s ally was from his people, the Israelites, and Pharaoh was Persian from Istakhr.
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {هذا من شيعته} [القصص: 15] قال: من قومه

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r3.claim: A report from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh and his associates identifies the ally as an Israelite and the enemy as a Copt.
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r3.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن أصحابه، " {هذا من شيعته} [القصص: 15] إسرائيلي {وهذا من عدوه} [القصص: 15] قبطي

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r4.claim: Mujahid explains وَكَزَهُ as striking with the gathered palm of the hand.
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {فوكزه موسى} [القصص: 15] قال: بجمع كفه

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r5.claim: Qatada says the prophet Moses did not intend to kill the man.

TAB-FULL:v18p189/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq likewise says Moses killed the man without intending to do so.
TAB-FULL:v18p189/r6.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: «قتله وهو لا يريد قتله»

TAB-FULL:v18p190/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p190/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p190/r1.claim: A report from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s associates says Moses buried the slain man in the sand.
TAB-FULL:v18p190/r1.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن أصحابه، " {فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه}

TAB-FULL:v18p190#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p190#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p190#2/r1.claim: Satan misleads by making ugly acts seem good; his manifest enmity and misguidance have been clear from long ago.
TAB-FULL:v18p190#2/r1.anchor: وتحسينه ذلك له {مبين} [البقرة: 168] يعني أنه يبين عداوته لهم قديما، وإضلاله إياهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r1.claim: ʿAlā ḥīni ghaflatin can be circumstantial of the subject, meaning Moses was there stealthily, or of the object.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r1.anchor: في موضع الحال [إما] من الفاعل: كائنا على حين غفلة أي: مستخفيا، وإما من المفعول.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r2.speaker: أبو طالب القارئ
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r2.claim: Abū Ṭālib al-Qāriʾ reads ḥīna with fatḥa; the Shaykh explains it by analogy with a verbal form after an adverb is annexed to it, citing a poem.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r2.anchor:
في أنه إذا أضيف الظرف إليه جاز بناؤه على الفتح كقوله:
3587 على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا

SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r3.claim: Min ahlihā describes ghafla, meaning the moment of heedlessness came from its people.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r3.anchor: و " من أهلها " صفة ل " غفلة " أي: صادرة من أهلها.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r4.claim: Yaqtatilān is an adjective describing two men; Ibn ʿAṭiyyah instead calls it a circumstantial clause, a construction Sibawayh permits more broadly than most grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r4.anchor: قوله: { يقتتلان } صفة ل " رجلين ". وقال ابن عطية: " حال منهما " وسيبويه وإن كان جوزها من النكرة/ مطلقا.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r5.speaker: نعيم بن ميسرة
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r5.claim: Nuʿaym ibn Maysarah reads yaqtulān with assimilation, shifting the first tāʾ's vowel to the qāf and merging the tāʾs.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15/r5.anchor: وقرأ نعيم بن ميسرة " يقتلان " بالإدغام نقل فتحة التاء الأولى إلى القاف وأدغم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r1.claim: Hādhā min shīʿatihi is a nominal clause describing the two men, or a circumstantial clause of the subject pronoun in yaqtatilān; the second is remote because the state does not change.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { هذا من شيعته } مبتدأ وخبر في موضع الصفة ل " رجلين " أو الحال من الضمير في " يقتتلان " وهو بعيد لعدم انتقالها.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r2.claim: The repeated demonstrative depicts the past scene as if present; al-Mubarrad says Arabs point with hādhā to absent people and cites Jarīr.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r2.anchor: وقال المبرد: " العرب تشير ب هذا إلى الغائب وأنشد الجرير:

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r3.claim: The common reading fastaghāthahu derives from ghawth and means he sought his aid and support.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r3.anchor: قوله: { فاستغاثه } هذه قراءة العامة، من الغوث أي: طلب غوثه ونصره.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh, Ibn Muqsim, and al-Zafrānī read with ʿayn and nūn, deriving the verb from assistance.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ سيبويه وابن مقسم والزعفراني بالعين المهملة، والنون، من الإعانة.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah calls the assistance reading a corruption; Ibn Jabbārah prefers Ibn Muqsim's reading because assistance better fits the context.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " هي تصحيف ". وقال ابن جبارة صاحب " الكامل ": " الاختيار قراءة ابن مقسم؛ لأن الإعانة أولى في هذا الباب ".

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r6.claim: The author says accusing these readers of corruption is unfair, while al-Hudhalī's excessive preference for an anomalous reading is also blameworthy.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#2/r6.anchor: قلت: نسبة التصحيف إلى هؤلاء غير محمودة، كما أن تعالي الهذلي في اختيار الشاذ غير محمود.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r1.claim: Wakz means striking or pushing with the whole palm; lakz is with the fingertips, though another view reverses the distinction, and nakz is like lakz.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r1.anchor: والفرق بين الوكز واللكز: أن الأول بجميع الكف، والثاني بأطراف الأصابع وقيل: بالعكس. والنكز كاللكز.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r2.claim: The cited poem uses nakz to mean a snake's sting or jab.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r2.anchor:
قال:
3589 يا أيها الجاهل ذو التنزي
لا توعدني حية بالنكز

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads fa-lakazahu and fa-nakazahu, with lām and nūn replacing the common verb.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود " فلكزه " و " فنكزه " باللام والنون.

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r4.claim: The subject of fa-qaḍā can be Moses, God, or the action itself, meaning the blow.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r4.anchor: قوله: { فقضى } أي: موسى، أو الله تعالى، أو ضمير الفعل أي: الوكز

SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r5.claim: Min ʿamal refers to Satan's whispering and inducement, namely the killing that resulted.
SAMIN-DURR:28:15#3/r5.anchor: قوله: { من عمل }: من وسوسته وتسويله والإشارة إلى القتل الصادر منه

TABATABAI:28:15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.claim: This section recounts events after Moses reached maturity that led him to leave Egypt for Midian.
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.anchor: فيه ذكر بعض ما وقع بعد بلوغه أشده فأدى إلى خروجه من مصر وقصده مدين

TABATABAI:28:15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r2.claim: The city is Egypt; Moses entered it from outside when its people were inattentive.
TABATABAI:28:15/r2.anchor: لا ريب أن المدينة التي دخلها على حين غفلة من أهلها هي مصر

TABATABAI:28:15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r3.claim: The later report of a man running from the far end of the city supports the inference that Pharaoh’s palace was outside it.
TABATABAI:28:15/r3.anchor: ويؤيد ما ذكرنا ما سيأتي من قوله { وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى }

TABATABAI:28:15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r4.claim: The city’s time of inattention is when people return indoors and markets and streets are empty, such as midday or the middle of the night.

TABATABAI:28:15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r5.claim: The two men were quarrelling and striking one another.

TABATABAI:28:15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r6.claim: The Israelite belonged to Moses’ religious party, which traced itself to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob but retained little beyond the name and outwardly worshipped Pharaoh; the opposing man was a Copt, an enemy of Israelites.
TABATABAI:28:15/r6.anchor: فإن بني إسرائيل كانوا ينتسبون يومئذ إلى آبائهم إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب عليهم السلام في دينهم

TABATABAI:28:15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r7.claim: Moses’ fear that the Egyptians would kill him for an earlier offense also supports identifying the opponent as a Copt.
TABATABAI:28:15/r7.anchor: ومن الشاهد أيضا على كون هذا الرجل قبطيا قوله في موضع آخر يخاطب ربه

TABATABAI:28:15/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r8.claim: The Israelite asked Moses to support him against his Coptic enemy; istighātha means seeking aid, from ghawth, meaning help.
TABATABAI:28:15/r8.anchor: الإستغاثة الاستنصار من الغوث بمعنى النصرة أي طلب الإسرائيلي من موسى أن ينصره

TABATABAI:28:15/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r9.claim: Wakz means thrusting, pushing, or striking with the gathered hand; the pronouns refer to the opposing man, whom Moses struck and killed.
TABATABAI:28:15/r9.anchor: والوكز - على ما ذكره الراغب وغيره - الطعن والدفع والضرب بجمع الكف

TABATABAI:28:15/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r10.claim: Qadāʾ means judgment, and saying Moses finished the man’s affair is a euphemism for his death.
TABATABAI:28:15/r10.anchor: والقضاء هو الحكم والقضاء عليه كناية عن الفراغ من أمره بموته

TABATABAI:28:15/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r11.claim: Moses’ blow killed the Copt by accident; an intentional killing would have been expressed with the word for killing.
TABATABAI:28:15/r11.anchor: وكان قتل خطأ ولو لا ذلك لكان من حق الكلام أن يعبر بالقتل

TABATABAI:28:15/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r12.claim: The phrase ‘this is Satan’s work’ points to the hostility and fight that culminated in the Copt’s death; min can mean kind or origin.
TABATABAI:28:15/r12.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية تفيد معنى الجنس أو نشوئية

TABATABAI:28:15/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r13.claim: Satan stirred enmity and fighting, drawing Moses into the conflict and the killing, which exposed him to grave danger.
TABATABAI:28:15/r13.anchor: فإنه هو الذي أوقع العداوة والبغضاء بينهما وأغرى على الاقتتال حتى أدى ذلك إلى مداخلة موسى

TABATABAI:28:15/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r14.claim: Moses knew the killing would become known and that the Copts, led by Pharaoh and his chiefs, would retaliate against him and anyone involved.
TABATABAI:28:15/r14.anchor: وقد كان يعلم أن الواقعة لا تبقى خفية مكتومة وأن القبط سيثورون عليه

TABATABAI:28:15-17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r1.claim: Moses realized his mistaken blow had put him in danger; he attributes the misstep to Satan because God guides only to truth and what is right.
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r1.anchor: أخطأ فيما فعله من الوكز الذي أورده مورد الهلكة ولا ينسب الوقوع في الخطأ إلى الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:28:15-17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r2.claim: The accidental blow was not a sin: Moses was defending an Israelite against an unjust unbeliever, though Satan can also lead people into non-sinful mistakes that cause hardship, as with Adam and his wife.
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r2.anchor: وإن لم يكن معصية منه لوقوعه خطأ وكون دفاعه عن الإسرائيلي دفعا لكافر ظالم

TABATABAI:28:15-17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r3.claim: Calling the event Satan’s work expresses Moses’ rejection and regret over the fight that caused the killing and grave danger.
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r3.anchor: انزجار منه عما وقع من الاقتتال المؤدي إلى قتل القبطي ووقوعه في عظيم الخطر وندم منه على ذلك

TABATABAI:28:15-17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r4.claim: Moses calls the act Satanic misguidance, meaning an error in judgment and course with dire consequences, not a culpable sin; his answer to Pharaoh later calls it misguidance.
TABATABAI:28:15-17/r4.anchor: سوء التدبير وضلال السعي يسوقه إلى عاقبة وخيمة

TABATABAI:28:17-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:17-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:17-18/r7.claim: The three successive ‘he said’ clauses mark different speech acts: judgment, prayer for forgiveness, and a binding commitment.
TABATABAI:28:17-18/r7.anchor: وقد كرر { قال } ثلاثا حيث قيل { قال هذا من عمل الشيطان } { قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي } { قال رب بما أنعمت علي } وذلك لاختلاف السياق

TABATABAI:28:15-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r1.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r1.claim: In al-Riḍā’s account, Moses killed the enemy by God’s command, while ‘Satan’s work’ refers to the fight between the men, not Moses’ killing.
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r1.anchor: فقضى على العدو بحكم الله تعالى ذكره فوكزه فمات، قال هذا من عمل الشيطان يعني الاقتتال الذي وقع بين الرجلين لا ما فعله موسى

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r1.claim: Tafsir places Moses’ entry into the city at midday, during the siesta.

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r2.claim: The two demonstratives this is from his party and this from his enemy describe absent people as if they were present in the scene.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r2.anchor: وجد فيها رجلين أحدهما من شيعته وأحدهما من عدوه

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r3.claim: Alternatively, the demonstratives narrate the scene as present: a viewer looking at the two men would say one is from his party and one from his enemy.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r3.anchor: على جهة الحكاية للحضرة، أي فوجد

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r4.claim: The man of Moses’ party was an Israelite, and the man of his enemy’s party was among Pharaoh’s people.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r4.anchor: من بني إسرائيل، والذي من عدوه من أصحاب فرعون

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r5.claim: Tafsir says Pharaoh was from Istakhr; the slain enemy is variously said to be a Copt or also from Istakhr.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r5.anchor: كان رجلا من أهل اصطخر، ويقال إن الرجل الذي هو من عدوه

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r6.claim: فاستغاثه means that the Israelite sought Moses’ aid or support.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r6.anchor: أي استنصره، والذي من شيعته من بني إسرائيل

ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r7.claim: فوكزه means Moses killed him by striking with the closed hand; some say he struck him with a stick.
ZAJJAJ:v4p136/r7.anchor: الوكز أن تضرب بجمع كفك، وقد قيل وكزه بالعصا

TABRISI:28:15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:28:15/r1.claim: Mujāhid says Moses pushed the man in the chest with his closed hand.
TABRISI:28:15/r1.anchor: فوكزه موسى } أي دفع في صدره بجمع كفه عن مجاهد

TABRISI:28:15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:15/r2.claim: Qatāda says Moses struck the man with his staff.

TABRISI:28:15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:15/r3.claim: Moses says the event was Satan's work because Satan incited his anger and provoked the blow.
TABRISI:28:15/r3.anchor: أي بسببه حتى هيج غضبي فضربته فهو من إغرائه.

TABRISI:28:15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:28:15/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says killing an unbeliever was not lawful then because the situation required refraining from fighting.
TABRISI:28:15/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: لم يكن يحل قتل الكافر يومئذ لأن الحال كانت حال الكف عن القتال

TABRISI:28:15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:28:15/r5.claim: Alternatively, the action that caused the killing came from Satan's whispering.
TABRISI:28:15/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن الأمر الذي وقع القتل بسببه من عمل الشيطان أي حصل بوسوسة الشيطان

TABRISI:28:15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r6.speaker: المرتضى
TABRISI:28:15/r6.claim: Al-Murtaḍā offers two further readings: Satan prompted Moses to kill instead of postponing it and losing the reward of a recommended act, or the victim's own conduct was Satanic and made him deserving of death.
TABRISI:28:15/r6.anchor: وذكر المرتضى قدس الله روحه فيه وجهين آخرين: أحدهما: أنه أراد أن تزيين قتلي له وتركي لما ندبت إليه من تأخيره

TABRISI:28:15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:15/r7.claim: Satan is the enemy of humanity and plainly misleads.
TABRISI:28:15/r7.anchor: ثم وصف الشيطان فقال { إنه عدو } لبني آدم { مضل مبين } ظاهر العداوة والإضلال

TABRISI:28:15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:15/r8.speaker: المعترضون
